```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.align = "center")
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))
derived <- Sys.getenv("LOY_REPORT_DERIVED")
rr <- function(name) { x <- readRDS(file.path(derived, paste0(name, ".rds"))); setDT(x); x }
js <- function(name) jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(derived, paste0(name, ".json")))
num <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
pv <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p < 1e-3, formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 1), formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)))
r2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
f3 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
show <- function(dt, ...) knitr::kable(dt, ...)

calls <- rr("y_status_calls")[Sex == "Male"]
cohort <- rr("cohort")
sizes <- rr("cohort_sizes")
validation <- js("call_validation")
genes <- rr("gene_pan_results")
gene_json <- js("gene_pan_summary")
hits <- genes[associated == TRUE][order(p)]
rnai <- rr("gene_pan_hits_rnai")
continuous <- rr("gene_pan_continuous")
drugs <- rr("drug_pan_results")
consensus <- rr("drug_pan_consensus")
mechanism <- rr("drug_pan_mechanism")
gene_ctx <- js("context_gene_summary")
drug_ctx <- js("context_drug_summary")
gene_ctx_summary <- rr("context_gene_summary")
ctx_cal <- rbind(rr("context_gene_calibration")[, outcome := "genes"], rr("context_drug_calibration")[, outcome := "drugs"])
ctx_hits <- rr("context_gene_hits")
ctx_robust <- rr("robustness_context_gene_hits")
heterogeneity <- rr("context_gene_lineage_heterogeneity")
de <- rr("expression_de_results")
de_json <- js("expression_de_summary")
dosage <- rr("expression_de_dosage_control")
de_pathways <- rr("expression_de_pathways")
dep_summary <- rr("expression_dependency_summary")
dep_set <- rr("expression_dependency_set")
attribution <- rr("expression_dependency_y_genes")
dep_top <- rr("expression_dependency_top")
overlap <- rr("expression_dependency_de_overlap")
accuracy <- rr("forest_expression_accuracy")
forest_features <- rr("forest_expression_features")
forest_null <- rr("forest_expression_null")
confounder <- rr("forest_confounders")
forest_y <- rbindlist(lapply(list.files(file.path(derived, "forest_y_status"), "^forest_y_status_summary_.*\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE), readRDS))
forest_y_genes <- { x <- readRDS(file.path(derived, "forest_y_status", "forest_y_status_crispr_effect.rds")); setDT(x); x }
robust <- rr("robustness_gene_hits")
by_definition <- rr("robustness_gene_scan_by_definition")
drug_by_definition <- rr("robustness_drug_scan_by_definition")
cmp_calls <- rr("comparison_call_agreement")
cmp_genes <- rr("comparison_gene_scan")
cmp_candidates <- rr("comparison_prior_candidates")
controls <- rr("pipeline_controls")
controls_json <- js("pipeline_controls")

n_neg <- sum(calls$y_call %in% "Y_negative"); n_pos <- sum(calls$y_call %in% "Y_positive"); n_aside <- sum(is.na(calls$y_call))
in_crispr <- cohort$ModelID %in% rownames(readRDS(file.path(derived, "matrices", "crispr_effect.rds")))
wgd_neg <- cohort[in_crispr & y_negative %in% 1, mean(WGD, na.rm = TRUE)]
wgd_all <- cohort[in_crispr & y_negative %in% 0, mean(WGD, na.rm = TRUE)]
wgd_one <- cohort[in_crispr & y_call_one_copy %in% "Y_positive", mean(WGD, na.rm = TRUE)]
within <- robust[check == "within lineage"]
definite <- calls[rna_call %in% c("depleted", "expressed") & dna_call %in% c("loss", "retained")]
n_agree <- sum((definite$rna_call == "depleted") == (definite$dna_call == "loss"))
crispr <- sizes[dataset == "crispr_effect"]
hit_symbols <- hits$symbol
paired <- attribution[paired == TRUE & dependency %in% hit_symbols]
best_drug <- drugs[which.min(p)]
shuffled <- function(outcome_name, column) paste(ctx_cal[outcome == outcome_name & run != "observed", sum(get(column)), by = run]$V1, collapse = ", ")
observed <- function(outcome_name, column) ctx_cal[outcome == outcome_name & run == "observed", sum(get(column))]
acc_wide <- dcast(accuracy, dependency ~ sub(" .*$", "", model), value.var = "r2_mean")
bh <- function(p) p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
# The X partners as their own pre-specified family, with their RNAi result.
partners <- merge(genes[!is.na(y_partner), .(symbol, y_partner, estimate, p)], rr("gene_pan_rnai")[, .(symbol, rnai_estimate = estimate, rnai_p = p)], by = "symbol", all.x = TRUE)
partners[, fdr_family := bh(p)]
extra_partners <- partners[!symbol %in% hit_symbols & fdr_family < 0.05][order(p)]
quiet_partners <- partners[!symbol %in% hit_symbols & fdr_family >= 0.05, symbol]
partner_text <- paste(sprintf("%s (%s, RNAi p = %s)", extra_partners$symbol, r2(extra_partners$estimate), ifelse(is.na(extra_partners$rnai_p), "not measured", pv(extra_partners$rnai_p))), collapse = ", ")
# PRISM secondary: tail of the p-values and direction of the nominal hits.
secondary <- drugs[dataset == "prism_secondary"]
secondary_tail <- sum(secondary$p < 0.001)
secondary_expected <- 0.001 * nrow(secondary)
secondary_positive <- secondary[p < 0.05, mean(estimate > 0)]
other_datasets <- drugs[dataset != "prism_secondary"]
screen_matrix <- readRDS(file.path(derived, "matrices", "prism_secondary_screen.rds"))
top_secondary <- secondary[order(p)][1:10]
hts_share <- vapply(top_secondary$feature, function(f) { v <- screen_matrix[[f]]; mean(v[!is.na(v)] == "HTS002") }, numeric(1))
# Alternative-definition drug hits, by compound.
alt_hits <- drug_by_definition[definition != "primary" & hits > 0, .(compound = unlist(strsplit(compounds, ";", fixed = TRUE))), by = .(dataset, definition)]
alt_counts <- alt_hits[, .(definitions = uniqueN(definition)), by = .(dataset, compound)][order(-definitions)]
n_alt_definitions <- uniqueN(drug_by_definition[definition != "primary", definition])
alt_text <- paste(sprintf("%s in %d", tolower(alt_counts$compound), alt_counts$definitions), collapse = " and ")
secondary_forest_features <- forest_y[dataset == "prism_secondary", features]
# Context screen: detectable interaction after correction for the number of tests in each class.
power_multiplier <- qnorm(0.975) + qnorm(0.8)
class_tests <- gene_ctx_summary[, .(class_tests = sum(tests)), by = class]
gene_ctx_summary <- merge(gene_ctx_summary, class_tests, by = "class")
gene_ctx_summary[, corrected_mde := median_interaction_mde / power_multiplier * (qnorm(1 - 0.05 / (2 * class_tests)) + qnorm(0.8))]
mde_nominal <- median(gene_ctx_summary$median_interaction_mde, na.rm = TRUE)
mde_corrected <- median(gene_ctx_summary$corrected_mde, na.rm = TRUE)
q_liberal <- heterogeneity[selective == TRUE, mean(q_p < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)]
# Earlier interaction candidates that have a counterpart test here (one row per distinct test).
earlier <- unique(cmp_candidates[grepl("interaction", test_type) & new_note != "not tested in the new analysis",
  .(name = fifelse(is.na(symbol) | symbol == "", compound_name, symbol), old_effect, new_dataset, new_context, new_estimate, new_p, new_fdr)], by = c("name", "new_dataset", "new_context"))
earlier[, same_direction_nominal := new_p < 0.05 & sign(new_estimate) == sign(old_effect)]
earlier_examples <- earlier[same_direction_nominal == TRUE][order(new_p)][1:min(3, sum(earlier$same_direction_nominal))]
# What the cancer-type tests could detect (stage 24).
power <- js("power_summary")
power_census <- rr("power_census")
power_types <- rr("power_cancer_types")
power_limits <- rr("power_limits")
power_shift <- rr("power_shift_detection")
power_bench <- rr("power_benchmarks")
power_detect <- rr("power_benchmark_detection")
power_null <- rr("power_benchmark_null")
power_levels <- merge(rr("power_benchmark_levels"), unique(rr("power_shift_detection")[, .(context_id, level, label)]), by = "context_id")
power_positive <- rr("power_positive_controls")
power_genotype <- rr("power_genotype_context_limits")
power_drugs <- rr("power_drug_limits")
level_names <- c(lineage = "Lineage", disease = "Primary disease", subtype = "Subtype")
level_plural <- c(lineage = "lineages", disease = "diseases", subtype = "subtypes")
census_of <- function(l) power_census[level == l]
n_types <- uniqueN(power_shift$context_id)
harmonic <- function(a, b) 1 / (1 / a + 1 / b)
# Shift found 80% of the time, per tested cancer type and bar; NA where no shift on the grid reaches 80%.
limit_of <- function(bar_name, grid_unit, target_value = 0.8) power_limits[bar == bar_name & unit == grid_unit & target == target_value]
one_chronos <- limit_of("one_type", "chronos")
run_chronos <- limit_of("as_run", "chronos")
one_sd <- limit_of("one_type", "sd")
run_sd <- limit_of("as_run", "sd")
largest_type <- one_chronos[which.min(limit)]
smallest_reached <- one_chronos[reachable == TRUE][which.max(limit)]
median_limit <- function(l) one_chronos[level == l, median(limit, na.rm = TRUE)]
never_one <- one_sd[reachable == FALSE]
never_run <- run_sd[reachable == FALSE]
names_of <- function(dt) paste(sprintf("%s (%d vs %d)", dt$label, dt$n_negative, dt$n_positive), collapse = ", ")
untestable <- power_types[status %in% c("below the gate", "one Y group missing")][order(-(n_negative + n_positive))]
# Normal-theory limit for the pan-cancer scan, for scale.
pan_limit <- (qnorm(1 - 0.05 / (2 * nrow(genes))) + qnorm(0.8)) * sqrt(1 / crispr$y_negative + 1 / crispr$y_positive) * power$gene_sd$median
formula <- one_sd[, .(context_id, label, n_negative, n_positive, as_analysed = limit, best_case, size = harmonic(n_negative, n_positive))][order(-size)]
formula_top <- formula[1:3]
# Benchmarks, moved into each cancer type as a copy of the benchmark gene.
detect_own <- power_detect[design == "own gene"]
detect_typical <- power_detect[design == "typical gene" & with_spread == TRUE]
detect_clean <- power_detect[design == "typical gene" & with_spread == FALSE]
reach_own <- merge(power_bench[, .(benchmark = label, class, effect)], detect_own[, .(types = sum(one_type >= 0.8), half = sum(one_type >= 0.5), as_run = sum(as_run >= 0.8), best = max(one_type)), by = benchmark], by = "benchmark")[order(-types, -best)]
reach_typical <- detect_typical[, .(types = sum(one_type >= 0.8), best = max(one_type)), by = benchmark]
types_finding <- function(name) reach_own[benchmark == name, types]
weak_best <- max(reach_typical[benchmark %in% power_bench[class %in% c("Paralog or synthetic lethal", "Collateral") & gene != "STAG1", label], types])
best_of <- function(name) reach_own[benchmark == name, best]
bench_at <- function(dt, name, type_label, type_level = "lineage") dt[benchmark == name & label == type_label & level == type_level, one_type]
level_of <- function(name, type_label) power_levels[benchmark == name & label == type_label & level == "lineage", gene_level]
# Does a benchmark's copy do worse where the gene is already more of a dependency? Rank correlation per benchmark, lineages only.
room <- merge(detect_own[level == "lineage", .(benchmark, context_id, one_type)], power_levels[, .(benchmark, context_id, gene_level)], by = c("benchmark", "context_id"))
room <- room[, .(spread = max(one_type) - min(one_type), rho = suppressWarnings(cor(gene_level, one_type, method = "spearman"))), by = benchmark][spread >= 0.5]
positive_by_level <- power_positive[, .(chances = .N, nominal = sum(inside_p < 0.05), alone = sum(own_fdr < 0.05), family = sum(inside_fdr_class < 0.05), none = uniqueN(context_id) - uniqueN(context_id[own_fdr < 0.05]), types = uniqueN(context_id), predicted = sum(predicted_one_type)), by = level]
positive_lineage <- power_positive[level == "lineage", .(alone = sum(own_fdr < 0.05), predicted = sum(predicted_one_type), everywhere = sum(predicted_everywhere_one_type)), by = symbol][match(hit_symbols, symbol)]
positive_seen <- sum(positive_lineage$alone)
positive_expected <- sum(positive_lineage$everywhere)
power_alone <- rr("power_alone_hits")
alone_other <- power_alone[established == FALSE]
named_chronos <- limit_of("candidate", "chronos")
run_reached <- run_chronos[reachable == TRUE]
ceiling_rise <- { w <- dcast(power_shift[unit == "sd" & shift %in% c(6, 10)], context_id ~ shift, value.var = "one_type"); max(w[["10"]] - w[["6"]]) }
called <- function(name) reach_own[benchmark == name, as_run]
strongest <- reach_own[class == "Oncogene addiction" & as_run > 0][order(-as_run), sub(" in .*$", "", benchmark)]
cancer_calls <- gene_ctx_summary[class %in% c("lineage", "disease", "subtype"), sum(context_specific)]
n_floor <- power_types[status == "tested", sum(!floor_reaches_one_type)]
genotype_one <- power_genotype[bar == "one_type" & target == 0.8]
genotype_example <- genotype_one[label == "TERT" & class == "amplification"]
drug_testable <- power_drugs[testable == TRUE]
drug_by_dataset <- drug_testable[, .(lineages = .N, median_limit = median(best_case_dataset_sd, na.rm = TRUE), braf = abs(braf_effect_sd[1]), would_find_braf = sum(best_case_dataset_sd < abs(braf_effect_sd), na.rm = TRUE)), by = dataset]

# Stages 25 to 30: organoids, RNAi and primary AML. Every object here carries an ext_ prefix.
ext_rr <- function(name) { x <- readRDS(file.path(derived, "extension", paste0(name, ".rds"))); setDT(x); x }
ext_js <- function(name) jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(derived, "extension", paste0(name, ".json")))
ext_list <- function(x, none = "none") if (length(x) == 0) none else if (length(x) == 1) x else paste(paste(head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), "and", tail(x, 1))
ext_short <- function(x) sub(" \\(.*$", "", x)
ext_shuffled <- function(dt, column) paste(dt[run != "observed"][[column]], collapse = ", ")
ext_pair <- function(a, b) sprintf("%d\u00a0/\u00a0%d", a, b)
ext_count_word <- function(n) if (n == 0) "none" else as.character(n)
ext_start <- function(n) if (n == 0) "None is" else if (n == 1) "One is" else paste(n, "are")
ext_r1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
# Names for print: drug names in lower case unless they are codes; contexts and genotype groups in words.
ext_drug <- function(x) { short <- ext_short(x); ifelse(grepl("^[A-Z][a-z]+$", short), tolower(short), short) }
ext_context_name <- function(class, label) {
  ifelse(class == "molecular_subtype" & grepl("_LoF$", label), paste(sub("_LoF$", "", label), "loss of function"),
    ifelse(class == "driver", paste(label, "driver mutation"),
      ifelse(class == "deletion", paste(label, "deletion"),
        ifelse(class == "amplification", paste(label, "amplification"),
          ifelse(label == "WGD", "genome doubling", gsub("_", " ", label))))))
}
ext_genotype_name <- function(x) ifelse(x == "WGD", "genome-doubled", ifelse(x == "Metastasis-derived", "metastasis-derived", paste0(x, "-altered")))
# Organoids.
ext_org <- ext_js("organoid_prepare_summary")
ext_org_scan <- ext_js("organoid_scan_summary")
ext_org_cohort <- ext_rr("organoid_cohort")
ext_org_primary <- ext_org_cohort[in_primary == TRUE]
ext_org_males <- ext_org_cohort[male == TRUE]
ext_org_pan <- ext_rr("organoid_pan_results")
ext_org_hits <- ext_org_pan[associated == TRUE][order(p)]
ext_org_next <- ext_org_pan[associated == FALSE][which.min(p)]
ext_org_types <- ext_rr("organoid_type_screen")
ext_org_cal <- ext_rr("organoid_calibration")
ext_org_controls <- ext_rr("organoid_controls")
ext_org_inside <- ext_rr("organoid_genotype_screen")[detected_inside_only == TRUE][order(inside_p)]
ext_org_checks <- ext_rr("organoid_hit_followup")[is_hit == TRUE]
ext_org_definitions <- ext_org_checks[check == "Y-status definition" & variant != "primary", uniqueN(variant)]
ext_org_permutation <- ext_org_checks[check %like% "permutation"]
ext_count <- function(type, value) ext_org_primary[OncotreeLineage == type & y_negative == value, .N]
ext_g <- function(gene) ext_org_pan[symbol == gene]
ext_in <- function(gene, type_name) ext_org_types[symbol == gene & type == type_name]
ext_tier <- function(tier) ext_org_males[y_tier %in% tier, .N]
ext_org_kept_dna <- ext_org_males[y_tier == "rna_led_dna_ambiguous" & rna_call == "depleted" & dna_y_retained > 0.5, .N]
ext_org_low_dna <- ext_org_males[y_tier == "rna_led_dna_ambiguous" & rna_call == "expressed" & dna_y_ratio < 0.2, .N]
ext_org_continuous <- ext_rr("organoid_continuous")[fdr < 0.05][order(p)]
# Screen quality by Y group, without the weights (which are themselves a function of screen quality).
ext_tpr_rank <- wilcox.test(TPR ~ y_negative, data = ext_org_primary, exact = FALSE)$p.value
ext_tpr_fit <- coef(summary(lm(TPR ~ factor(OncotreeLineage) + LibraryV1 + MSI + y_negative, data = ext_org_primary)))["y_negative", ]
ext_ctl <- function(g) ext_org_controls[gene == g]
ext_msi <- function(value) ext_org_primary[OncotreeLineage == "Colorectal" & y_negative == value, sprintf("%d of %d", sum(MSI), .N)]
ext_panel <- ext_org_scan$genotype_contexts
ext_panel[ext_panel == "WGD"] <- "genome doubling"
ext_panel[ext_panel == "Metastasis-derived"] <- "metastatic origin"
# RNAi.
ext_rnai <- ext_js("rnai_context_run_summary")
ext_rnai_inside <- ext_rr("rnai_context_inside_only")
ext_rnai_by_gene <- ext_rnai_inside[, .N, by = symbol][order(-N)]
ext_rnai_types <- ext_rr("rnai_context_focused")[class %in% c("lineage", "disease", "subtype") & inside_fdr_focused < 0.05][order(inside_p)]
ext_rnai_type_text <- if (nrow(ext_rnai_types) == 0) "no paired gene passes inside a cancer type" else paste(ext_rnai_types[, .(text = sprintf("%s also passes inside %s", symbol[1], ext_list(tolower(label)))), by = symbol]$text, collapse = "; ")
ext_rnai_cal <- ext_rr("rnai_context_calibration")[, .(inside = sum(inside_fdr_class_hits), specific = sum(context_specific)), by = run]
ext_rnai_shared <- sum(in_crispr & !is.na(cohort$y_negative) & cohort$ModelID %in% rownames(readRDS(file.path(derived, "matrices", "rnai.rds"))))
# Cell lines and organoids combined.
ext_comb <- ext_js("combined_summary")
ext_pan <- ext_rr("combined_pan")
ext_pan_hits <- ext_pan[combined_hit == TRUE][order(combined_p)]
ext_both <- ext_pan_hits[evidence == "supported by both", symbol]
ext_one <- ext_pan_hits[evidence == "carried by one source", symbol]
ext_within <- ext_rr("combined_within_type")
ext_col <- "Colorectal adenocarcinoma"
ext_oes <- "Oesophagogastric adenocarcinoma"
ext_best <- function(label) ext_within[pair == label][which.min(combined_p)]
ext_share <- function(label) ext_within[pair == label, median((1 / organoid_unit^2) / (1 / organoid_unit^2 + 1 / cell_unit^2))]
ext_cross <- ext_rr("combined_cross_assay_summary")
ext_leads <- ext_rr("combined_cell_line_leads_in_rnai")
ext_leads_agree <- ext_leads[tested_in_rnai == TRUE & rnai_inside_p < 0.05 & sign(rnai_inside) == sign(crispr_inside)]
ext_leads_other <- ext_leads[tested_in_rnai == FALSE & symbol != "EIF1AX"]
ext_seen <- ext_rr("combined_seen_before")
ext_power <- ext_rr("extension_power")
ext_pw <- function(a, s) ext_power[analysis == a & source == s]
ext_lung <- one_sd[which.min(limit)]
ext_oes_lines <- cohort[in_crispr & !is.na(y_negative) & OncotreePrimaryDisease == "Esophagogastric Adenocarcinoma"]
# Primary AML.
ext_aml <- ext_js("beataml_prepare_summary")
ext_aml_scan <- ext_js("beataml_scan_summary")
ext_aml_all <- ext_rr("beataml_cohort")[in_primary == TRUE]
ext_aml_screen <- ext_aml_all[!is.na(age)]
ext_aml_high <- ext_aml_screen[f >= 0.5]
ext_aml_drugs <- ext_rr("beataml_drug_results")
ext_aml_hits <- ext_aml_drugs[associated == TRUE][order(p)]
ext_lead <- ext_aml_drugs[which.min(p)]
ext_aml_follow <- ext_rr("beataml_hit_followup")[inhibitor == ext_lead$inhibitor]
ext_fu <- function(text) ext_aml_follow[variant %like% text][1]
ext_aml_checks <- ext_aml_follow[!check %like% "added after|leave one|permutation" & !variant %like% "^main"]
ext_aml_weakest <- ext_aml_checks[which.max(p)]
ext_aml_controls <- ext_rr("beataml_controls")
ext_aml_cal <- ext_rr("beataml_calibration")
ext_aml_families <- ext_rr("beataml_family_results")
ext_mek_family <- ext_aml_families[family == "STE7 family"]
ext_aml_compare <- ext_rr("beataml_cell_line_comparison_summary")
ext_aml_ras <- ext_rr("beataml_ras_by_y_loss")
ext_ras_high <- ext_aml_ras[y_loss == "f at least 0.5"]
ext_ras_mid <- ext_aml_ras[y_loss == "f above the floor"]
ext_ras_none <- ext_aml_ras[y_loss == "no Y loss"]
ext_t821 <- function(high) ext_aml_screen[(f >= 0.5) == high, sprintf("%d of %d", sum(t8_21), .N)]
ext_aml_power <- ext_rr("beataml_power")
ext_mek <- ext_aml_drugs[inhibitor %like% "Trametinib|CI-1040"][order(p)]
ext_sensitive <- ext_aml_drugs[estimate < 0][which.min(p)]
# Stages 31 to 33: DepMap NextGen as a third CRISPR source. Every object here carries an ng_ prefix.
ng_prep <- ext_js("nextgen_prepare_summary")
ng_scan <- ext_js("nextgen_scan_summary")
ng_comb <- ext_js("nextgen_combined_summary")
ng_cohort <- ext_rr("nextgen_cohort")
ng_primary <- ng_cohort[in_primary == TRUE]
ng_eligible <- ng_cohort[eligible == TRUE]
ng_males <- ng_cohort[recorded_male == TRUE]
ng_all_males <- ext_rr("nextgen_y_calls")[recorded_male == TRUE]
ng_donors <- ext_rr("nextgen_donor_groups")
ng_pan <- ext_rr("nextgen_pan_results")
ng_paired <- ext_rr("nextgen_paired_genes")
ng_null <- ext_rr("nextgen_calibration")[run != "observed"]
ng_runs <- nrow(ng_null)
ng_controls <- ext_rr("nextgen_controls")
ng_types <- ext_rr("nextgen_type_screen")
ng_follow <- ext_rr("nextgen_hit_followup")[context == "All models"]
ng_continuous <- ext_rr("nextgen_continuous")[fdr < 0.05][order(p)]
ng_three <- ext_rr("nextgen_combined_pan")
ng_three_hits <- ng_three[combined_hit == TRUE][order(combined_p)]
ng_three_follow <- ext_rr("nextgen_combined_followup")
ng_hits <- ext_rr("nextgen_combined_hits")
ng_pooled_all <- ext_rr("nextgen_pooled_type")
ng_within <- ext_rr("nextgen_combined_within_type")
ng_pooled_named <- ext_rr("nextgen_pooled_named")
ng_sensitivity <- ext_rr("nextgen_pooled_sensitivity")
ng_shared <- ext_rr("nextgen_shared_donors")
ng_power <- ext_rr("nextgen_power")
ng_counts <- ext_rr("nextgen_pooled_types")
ng_rnai <- rr("gene_pan_rnai")
```

# Summary

This is a new analysis of chromosome-Y loss in male DepMap 26Q1 cell lines, built from the raw tables and independent of the three September analyses in this collection. It asks which gene dependencies and drug sensitivities go with Y loss across cancers, which of those depend on context, and which genes' expression is associated with the dependencies.

- **Y status.** Of `r num(nrow(calls))` annotated male lines, `r n_neg` are Y-negative, `r n_pos` are Y-positive and `r n_aside` are set aside. The call leads with RNA (seven Y genes) and uses DNA copy number as support; where both are definite they agree in `r n_agree` of `r nrow(definite)` lines.
- **Dependencies.** Comparing `r crispr$y_negative` Y-negative with `r crispr$y_positive` Y-positive lines, `r nrow(hits)` of `r num(nrow(genes))` genes pass FDR 0.05: `r paste(hit_symbols, collapse = ", ")`. Each is the X-linked partner of a Y gene, each survives adjustment for genome doubling, TP53 status and aneuploidy, and each holds under all nine Y-status definitions tried. No other gene passes.
- **Drugs.** No compound passes FDR 0.05 in any of `r uniqueN(drugs$dataset)` dataset-screens (`r num(nrow(drugs))` tests), in a model that pools `r nrow(consensus)` compounds across datasets, or as a mechanism or target class. The closest is `r tolower(best_drug$compound_name)` (FDR `r f3(best_drug$fdr)` in PRISM secondary). It passes under some alternative Y-status definitions but is not reproduced in a second screen of the same compound, and PRISM secondary as a whole shows a small shift that looks like a screen effect.
- **Context.** Across `r num(gene_ctx$screen_tests)` gene and `r num(drug_ctx$tests)` drug interaction tests the screens made `r gene_ctx$screen_context_specific` and `r drug_ctx$context_specific` context-specific calls. Shuffling Y status gives the same yield, so the context screens show nothing beyond chance. The four hits are not specific to a lineage or genotype, although the size of the DDX3X and EIF1AX effects varies between lineages.
- **What the cancer-type tests could have found.** Enough lines to test exist for `r census_of('lineage')$at_least_5` of `r census_of('lineage')$with_lines` lineages, but for only `r census_of('disease')$at_least_5` of `r census_of('disease')$with_lines` primary diseases and `r census_of('subtype')$at_least_5` of `r census_of('subtype')$with_lines` subtypes. For a gene named in advance, a shift of about `r r2(median(named_chronos$limit))` Chronos units inside one cancer type would be found 80% of the time. Genome-wide it had to reach `r r2(largest_type$limit)` (`r largest_type$label`) to `r r2(smallest_reached$limit)` (`r smallest_reached$label`) with the cancer type analysed alone, and under the screen's own rule `r nrow(never_run)` of the `r n_types` tested cancer types have no effect size that is found that often. An effect like BRAF dependency in BRAF V600E lines would have been called by the screen in `r called('BRAF in BRAF V600E')` of the `r n_types`. Of `r nrow(reach_own)` known vulnerabilities, `r sum(reach_own$as_run == 0)` would have been called in none (`r reach_own[types == 0, .N]` with the cancer type analysed alone, `r sum(reach_typical$types == 0)` when the same effect sits on an ordinary gene).
- **Other models.** Three public sources were added on 2026-10-04. In `r nrow(ext_org_primary)` male organoids (`r sum(ext_org_primary$y_negative == 1)` Y-negative, `r sum(ext_org_primary$y_negative == 0)` Y-positive), `r nrow(ext_org_hits)` of `r num(nrow(ext_org_pan))` genes pass, `r ext_list(ext_org_hits$symbol)`; ZFX does not, and EIF1AX is not in the organoid library. With the organoids, the effect detectable genome-wide in colorectal and oesophagogastric cancer falls from about `r ext_r1(ext_pw(ext_col, "Cell lines")$genome_wide)` SD to about `r ext_r1(ext_pw(ext_col, "Combined")$genome_wide)` SD, and `r if (sum(ext_within$combined_hit) == 0) "no gene passes" else paste(sum(ext_within$combined_hit), "pass")` in either. RNAi shows `r if (ext_rnai$screen_context_specific == 0) "nothing" else ext_rnai$screen_context_specific` context-specific. In primary AML, `r nrow(ext_aml_hits)` of `r nrow(ext_aml_drugs)` inhibitors passes, `r ext_list(ext_drug(ext_aml_hits$inhibitor))`, which is less active with Y loss; the association weakens once RAS-pathway mutations are in the model. DepMap NextGen was added as a fourth source on 2026-10-05. In `r nrow(ng_primary)` male models (`r ng_n(ng_primary, 1)` Y-negative, `r ng_n(ng_primary, 0)` Y-positive), `r ext_list(ng_confirmed)` replicate. `r ext_list(ng_unconfirmed)` has the right sign but is not confirmed (p = `r f3(ng_pg("ZFX")$p)` in the model, `r f3(ng_pg("ZFX")$permutation_p)` by permutation). No other gene is called. With the three CRISPR sources together the four still pass, and `r nrow(ng_extra)` more genes cross FDR 0.05 with small effects, `r ext_list(ng_extra$symbol)`. Neither is a vulnerability of Y loss, and neither stays a hit once NextGen's model carries genome doubling, TP53 and aneuploidy. Pooled across sources, `r ext_list(ng_pool_holds)` also show the Y effect inside `r ng_pool_name`.
- **Driver status inside cancer types.** Added on 2026-10-06. Of `r num(dt_cells("lineage")$pairs)` pairs of a driver gene and a lineage with an altered line, `r dt_cells("lineage")$at_least_5` have `r dt_word(dt_gate)` altered lines per Y group and `r dt_cells("lineage")$all_four_cells` can test whether the Y effect differs by driver status. Over the three levels that makes `r nrow(dt_splits)` splits. None of `r num(dt_tests$inside_tests)` tests among altered lines and `r num(dt_tests$interaction_tests)` tests of a difference passes, and the smallest p-values are the four paired genes. A gene named in advance needs a shift of about `r dt_r1(median(dt_lim("candidate")$limit))` SD. A search needs several SD: the layer's rank-based test reaches `r dt_pct(dt_target)`% detection in `r dt_reach("family")` of the `r nrow(dt_splits)` splits, at `r dt_r1(median(dt_fam$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD, and a test on the Chronos scale would need about `r dt_r1(median(dt_raw$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD. For effects like the known ones, the median split would need from `r dt_median(dt_known("DDX3X in Y-negative", "typical gene"))` to `r dt_multiple(max(dt_paired_multiples("own spread")))` times its lines, depending on how variable the gene is.
- **Expression.** Dependency on each X gene tracks expression of its own Y partner: with all seven Y genes in one model, the paired gene is the strongest term for all `r nrow(paired)` hits, and the relationship is graded even among lines that still express the Y. Outside chrY, `r de_json$de` genes differ in expression between the groups, led by pseudoautosomal genes, which fall by about `r r2(abs(dosage[dosage_class == "PAR", median_log_fc]))` log2 units as the loss of one of two copies predicts.
- **Forests.** Random forests agree with the regressions. A genome-wide forest that predicts Y status from dependencies confirms `r forest_y[dataset == "crispr_effect", stable]` genes, the same four, and none on shuffled labels; no compound is confirmed in any drug dataset. Y status and Y-gene expression predict the four dependencies, and the wider transcriptome adds only for ZFX.

In short: with every eligible line included, Y loss creates four strong, specific dependencies on X-linked paralogs. These data show no drug sensitivity and no context-specific vulnerability large enough to detect. Organoids confirm two of the four dependencies and add none. NextGen models confirm `r ext_list(ng_confirmed)` and not `r ext_list(ng_unconfirmed)`, and three CRISPR sources together add no vulnerability. Splitting cancer types by driver status adds none either; a search over the `r nrow(dt_splits)` splits that can be tested would have seen only shifts of several SD.

# What was compared

```{r tiers}
tier_names <- c(concordant = "RNA and DNA agree", dna_only = "DNA only (no RNA)", rna_only = "RNA only (no DNA)", rna_led_dna_ambiguous = "RNA definite, DNA partial or mosaic",
  rna_intermediate = "RNA intermediate", dna_ambiguous_no_rna = "DNA partial or mosaic, no RNA", no_data = "no RNA or DNA", discordant = "RNA and DNA disagree")
tiers <- calls[, .(`Y-negative` = sum(y_call %in% "Y_negative"), `Y-positive` = sum(y_call %in% "Y_positive"), `Set aside` = sum(is.na(y_call))), by = y_tier]
tiers[, Evidence := tier_names[y_tier]]
show(tiers[match(names(tier_names), y_tier), .(Evidence, `Y-negative`, `Y-positive`, `Set aside`)], caption = "Male lines by the evidence behind the call.")
```

```{r fig1}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig1_y_status_calls.png")
```

**How Y status was called.** The RNA score is the mean log2(TPM+1) of DDX3Y, EIF1AY, KDM5D, RPS4Y1, USP9Y, UTY and ZFY. Annotated female lines, which have no Y, set the reference: none of `r validation$females_with_rna` exceeds 1.0. A male line is *depleted* at a mean of 1.0 or less with at most one gene above its female maximum, and *expressed* at 2.5 or more with at least six genes above. The DNA call uses the relative copy ratio of the same genes (whole-genome sequencing where available, otherwise exome): loss at 0.03 or below, retained at 0.20 or above. RNA decides; DNA fills in where RNA is missing, and a clear disagreement sets the line aside.

Three points about this definition matter for reading the results.

- **The `r sum(calls$y_tier == "rna_intermediate")` RNA-intermediate lines are mostly real partial deletions**, for example loss of Yq with RPS4Y1 and ZFY retained. They are neither Y-negative nor intact, so they leave the two-group comparison, but they are used in the expression analyses, where they are the most informative lines.
- **Controls are every Y-positive male, Y-gain included.** Among CRISPR-screened lines this gives `r crispr$y_positive` controls instead of the `r by_definition[definition == "one_copy_controls", y_positive]` with a one-copy estimate, and their genome-doubling rate (`r round(100 * wgd_all)`%) is closer to that of Y-negative lines (`r round(100 * wgd_neg)`%) than the one-copy controls' is (`r round(100 * wgd_one)`%).
- **Calls are stable.** `r sum(!calls$call_stable)` of `r num(nrow(calls))` males change call when every threshold is moved by 20%. All `r validation$rna_depleted_wgs_definite` RNA-depleted lines with a definite whole-genome call are DNA losses.

**Who is in the comparison.** Eligible lines are annotated male, from a cancer, and not engineered: `r num(nrow(cohort))` lines, `r sum(cohort$in_primary)` with a call. All models of a donor are kept and the donor is a blocking factor. Lineage is a covariate in every model.

```{r sizes}
labels <- c(crispr_effect = "CRISPR (Chronos)", rnai = "RNAi (DEMETER2)", expr_tpm_pc = "Expression", prism_REPPRIMARY = "PRISM REP.PRIMARY", prism_REP1M = "PRISM REP.1M",
  prism_REP300 = "PRISM REP.300", prism_secondary = "PRISM secondary", gdsc1 = "GDSC1", gdsc2 = "GDSC2", ctrp = "CTRP v2")
show(sizes[match(names(labels), dataset), .(Assay = labels[dataset], `Y-negative` = y_negative, `Y-positive` = y_positive, `Set aside` = set_aside)], caption = "Eligible male lines per assay.")
```

Y-negative lines differ from Y-positive lines in ways that could mimic a Y effect, which is why every hit is re-tested with these as covariates.

```{r confounders}
conf <- cohort[in_primary == TRUE, .(`Genome doubled` = mean(WGD, na.rm = TRUE), `TP53 altered` = mean(tp53_altered, na.rm = TRUE), `LOH fraction` = mean(LoHFraction, na.rm = TRUE),
  `Aneuploidy score` = mean(Aneuploidy, na.rm = TRUE), `KY CRISPR library` = mean(LibraryKY, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(Group = fifelse(y_negative == 1, "Y-negative", "Y-positive"))]
show(conf, digits = 2, caption = "Group means of the main confounders (fractions, except the aneuploidy score).")
```

# Gene dependencies across cancers

```{r fig2}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig2_pan_cancer_genes.png")
```

```{r hits}
tab <- merge(hits, rnai[, .(symbol, rnai_estimate, rnai_p)], by = "symbol", sort = FALSE)
show(tab[, .(Gene = symbol, `Y partner` = y_partner, Effect = r2(estimate), FDR = pv(fdr), `Adjusted effect` = r2(estimate_adjusted),
  `Dependent, Y-neg` = paste0(round(100 * fraction_dependent_negative), "%"), `Dependent, Y-pos` = paste0(round(100 * fraction_dependent_positive), "%"),
  `RNAi effect` = ifelse(is.na(rnai_estimate), "not in table", r2(rnai_estimate)), `RNAi p` = pv(rnai_p))],
  caption = "Hits at FDR 0.05. Effect: Chronos score, Y-negative minus Y-positive. Adjusted: with genome doubling, TP53 and aneuploidy added. Dependent: dependency probability of at least 0.5.")
```

- **Model.** Chronos effect on lineage, CRISPR library and Y status, fitted by limma with donor blocking; `r num(nrow(genes))` autosomal and X genes, one FDR family.
- **Nothing else passes.** `r sum(genes$fdr < 0.05)` genes are below FDR 0.05 and `r sum(genes$fdr < 0.25)` below 0.25. The test statistics are close to their null (inflation factor `r r2(gene_json$lambda)`), and there is no overall shift in common-essential genes between the groups (difference `r formatC(gene_json$essential_shift$estimate, format = "f", digits = 3)`, p = `r pv(gene_json$essential_shift$p)`).
- **The other X partners, tested as their own family.** Among the `r nrow(partners)` pre-specified X partners of Y genes, `r nrow(extra_partners)` more pass FDR 0.05 within that family: `r partner_text`. These effects are small and none is reproduced in RNAi, so they are weak candidates; `r paste(quiet_partners, collapse = ", ")` show nothing. On the continuous Y-expression score, which uses all `r gene_json$continuous_lines` males with RNA, KDM5C also passes genome-wide (FDR `r pv(continuous[symbol == "KDM5C", fdr])`).
- **RNAi agrees.** In `r gene_json$rnai_lines` lines with RNAi data, `r gene_json$hits_rnai_replicated` of the `r gene_json$hits_with_rnai` hits present in that table replicate with the same sign.

## Robustness of the four hits

```{r fig3}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig3_gene_hit_robustness.png")
```

```{r definitions}
definition_names <- c(primary = "primary call", concordant_only = "RNA and DNA agree only", rna_only = "RNA only", dna_only = "DNA only", one_copy_controls = "one-copy controls only",
  no_relative_gain = "relative Y gain removed", lenient_rna_rule = "lenient RNA rule", xist_high_removed = "XIST-high lines removed", threshold_stable_only = "threshold-stable calls only")
show(by_definition[, .(Definition = definition_names[definition], Lines = lines, `Y-negative` = y_negative, `Y-positive` = y_positive, `Hits at FDR 0.05` = hits, Genes = gsub(";", ", ", genes))],
  caption = "The genome-wide scan repeated under each Y-status definition.")
```

```{r robustness-numbers}
perm <- robust[check == "permutation within lineage" & symbol %in% hit_symbols]
loo <- robust[check == "leave one lineage out" & symbol %in% hit_symbols]
conf_hits <- confounder[role == "hit"]
conf_null <- confounder[role != "hit"]
```

- **Definitions.** The same four genes pass under every definition, including DNA-only calls, RNA-only calls, concordant calls only, one-copy controls only, the lenient RNA rule, and with XIST-high lines removed.
- **Permutation.** Shuffling Y status within lineage 20,000 times never produced a statistic as large as the observed one for any hit (p = `r pv(max(perm$p))`, the smallest value that many shuffles can give).
- **Lineages.** Dropping any one lineage leaves every effect with the same sign; the smallest leave-one-lineage-out effects are `r paste(sprintf("%s %s", hit_symbols, r2(sapply(hit_symbols, function(s) loo[symbol == s][which.min(abs(estimate)), estimate]))), collapse = ", ")`.
- **Flexible adjustment.** In a forest that can also use lineage, library, genome doubling, TP53, aneuploidy, LOH, ploidy, MSI, CIN and screen quality, real Y status beats confounder-matched shuffled copies of itself in at least 80% of subsamples for `r sum(conf_hits$survives)` of `r nrow(conf_hits)` genes checked (`r paste(conf_hits[survives == TRUE, symbol], collapse = ", ")`). The same test passes for `r sum(conf_null$survives)` of `r nrow(conf_null)` random non-hit genes.

# Drug sensitivities across cancers

```{r fig4}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig4_pan_cancer_drugs.png")
```

```{r drugs}
dataset_names <- c(prism_REPPRIMARY = "PRISM REP.PRIMARY", prism_REP1M = "PRISM REP.1M", prism_REP300 = "PRISM REP.300", prism_secondary = "PRISM secondary", gdsc1 = "GDSC1", gdsc2 = "GDSC2", ctrp = "CTRP v2")
per <- drugs[, .(Compounds = .N, `FDR < 0.05` = sum(fdr < 0.05), `Smallest FDR` = f3(min(fdr)), `Top compound` = tolower(compound_name[which.min(p)])), by = dataset]
per <- merge(per, sizes[, .(dataset, `Y-negative` = y_negative, `Y-positive` = y_positive)], by = "dataset")
show(per[match(names(dataset_names), dataset), .(Dataset = dataset_names[dataset], `Y-negative`, `Y-positive`, Compounds, `FDR < 0.05`, `Smallest FDR`, `Top compound`)],
  caption = "Per-dataset scans: response on lineage and Y status, donor-clustered robust errors.")
```

- **No main effect in any dataset.** The p-values follow the null line in six of the seven panels (`r sum(other_datasets$p < 0.001)` compounds below 0.001 across them, against `r r2(0.001 * nrow(other_datasets))` expected).
- **PRISM secondary shows a small shift.** It has `r secondary_tail` compounds below p = 0.001 against `r r2(secondary_expected)` expected, and `r round(100 * secondary_positive)`% of its compounds with p < 0.05 have Y-negative lines *less* sensitive. The ten strongest were read mostly in the older HTS002 screen (median `r round(100 * median(hts_share))`% of their lines), and most are not anticancer agents (for example rifampin, estrone and bumetanide). That pattern points to a batch or screen effect rather than to specific pharmacology.
- **Pooling across datasets does not help.** For `r nrow(consensus)` compounds measured in more than one dataset family (GDSC1 and GDSC2 count as separate families), a mixed model with the cell line as a random effect gives a smallest FDR of `r r2(min(consensus$fdr, na.rm = TRUE))` (`r tolower(consensus[which.min(p), compound_name])`). Most drug-profiled lines appear in several datasets, so a plain meta-analysis would count them more than once.
- **No mechanism or target class.** Of `r nrow(mechanism)` classes with at least five compounds, tested against `r num(js("drug_pan_summary")$permutations)` within-lineage shuffles, none passes FDR 0.05 (smallest `r r2(min(mechanism$fdr))`). With that many shuffles the smallest attainable p is `r pv(1 / (js("drug_pan_summary")$permutations + 1))`, too large for a single class to pass on its own; the smallest observed p was `r pv(min(mechanism$p))`, well above that floor.
- **The nearest miss does not replicate.** `r tolower(best_drug$compound_name)` in PRISM secondary has Y-negative lines *less* sensitive (FDR `r f3(best_drug$fdr)`, `r best_drug$n_negative` vs `r best_drug$n_positive` lines). Under the `r n_alt_definitions` alternative Y-status definitions, PRISM secondary compounds pass FDR 0.05 as follows: `r alt_text` definitions. The same compound in the PRISM primary screen shows no effect (p = `r pv(drugs[dataset == "prism_REPPRIMARY" & compound_name == best_drug$compound_name, p][1])`), and both sit inside the screen-wide shift described above.
- **Forests agree, with a coverage caveat.** Drug responses predict Y status no better than lineage alone, and no compound is selected in any dataset. The forests use only compounds measured in at least 90% of lines; in PRISM secondary that is `r secondary_forest_features` of `r nrow(secondary)` compounds, which excludes both compounds above.

```{r drug-power}
z_power <- qnorm(0.8)
mde <- drugs[, .(nominal = (qnorm(0.975) + z_power) * median(se / response_sd), corrected = (qnorm(1 - 0.05 / (2 * .N)) + z_power) * median(se / response_sd)), by = dataset]
```

**What the scan could see.** With these group sizes a typical compound would show a difference of `r r2(min(mde$nominal))` to `r r2(max(mde$nominal))` response standard deviations at a nominal 0.05 with 80% power, and `r r2(min(mde$corrected))` to `r r2(max(mde$corrected))` after correcting for the number of compounds in the dataset. Smaller effects, or effects confined to a subset of lines, are not excluded.

# Context-specific interactions

```{r fig5}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig5_context_screen.png")
```

For each context the model adds the context and its interaction with Y status; the interaction is the test of context dependence. For a binary context a context-specific call also needs a significant Y effect inside the context. A continuous context (CIN, ploidy, aneuploidy, LOH fraction) has no inside group, so its calls rest on the interaction alone. The panel covers `r gene_ctx$contexts_fitted` contexts for genes: lineages, diseases and subtypes, DepMap's inferred molecular subtypes, driver genes with at least 20 altered lines, amplifications and deep deletions, genome doubling, MSI, and continuous CIN, ploidy, aneuploidy and LOH fraction. A context is fitted when every Y-by-context cell has at least five lines.

```{r context}
ctx_tab <- data.table(
  Screen = c("Gene dependencies", "Drug responses"),
  Tests = c(num(gene_ctx$screen_tests), num(drug_ctx$tests)),
  `Interactions at class FDR 0.05` = c(observed("genes", "interaction_fdr_class_hits"), observed("drugs", "interaction_fdr_class_hits")),
  `Same, five shuffles` = c(shuffled("genes", "interaction_fdr_class_hits"), shuffled("drugs", "interaction_fdr_class_hits")),
  `Context-specific calls` = c(observed("genes", "context_specific"), observed("drugs", "context_specific")),
  `Same, five shuffles ` = c(shuffled("genes", "context_specific"), shuffled("drugs", "context_specific"))
)
show(ctx_tab, caption = "Yield of the context screens on the real labels and on five shuffles of Y status within lineage and context level.")
```

- **The screens return what chance returns.** The observed counts sit inside the range of the shuffled runs for both genes and drugs.
- **The four hits are not context-specific.** In the focused family of the hits and the other X partners against every context (`r num(gene_ctx$focused_tests)` tests), no interaction passes.
- **Effect size does vary by lineage for two of them.** Cochran's Q across `r heterogeneity[symbol == "DDX3X", lineages]` lineages is significant for DDX3X (p = `r pv(heterogeneity[symbol == "DDX3X", q_p])`) and EIF1AX (p = `r pv(heterogeneity[symbol == "EIF1AX", q_p])`) but not for ZFX (p = `r pv(heterogeneity[symbol == "ZFX", q_p])`) or RPS4X (p = `r pv(heterogeneity[symbol == "RPS4X", q_p])`). The Q test runs somewhat liberal here (`r round(100 * q_liberal)`% of selective genes reach p < 0.05), so this is moderate evidence. The direction never changes: the within-lineage effect runs from `r r2(within[symbol == "DDX3X", max(estimate)])` to `r r2(within[symbol == "DDX3X", min(estimate)])` for DDX3X and from `r r2(within[symbol == "EIF1AX", max(estimate)])` to `r r2(within[symbol == "EIF1AX", min(estimate)])` for EIF1AX (Figure 3b). So the dependency is present everywhere and differs in size, which a one-lineage-against-the-rest test at these sample sizes did not pick up.
- **One candidate.** `r ctx_hits$symbol[1]` with `r ctx_hits$label[1]` is the screen's single call (interaction p = `r pv(ctx_hits$interaction_p[1])`). CIN is continuous, so the call rests on the interaction alone. It is stable to leaving out any line, to RNA-only and DNA-only calls and to adjustment for genome doubling, TP53 and aneuploidy (permutation p = `r pv(ctx_robust$permutation_p[1])`), but RNAi does not reproduce it (p = `r pv(ctx_robust$replication_p[1])`) and one shuffled run produced a call of the same kind. Treat it as a lead, not a finding.
- **What the screen could see.** By the normal-theory formula, the smallest interaction detectable with 80% power in a typical context was about `r r2(mde_nominal)` Chronos units at a nominal 0.05, and about `r r2(mde_corrected)` after correcting for the number of tests in its class (Figure 5c). That is larger than the whole ZFX effect (`r r2(genes[symbol == "ZFX", estimate])`), and it is a best case: the formula uses raw-scale standard errors, and the test that was run is rank-based. The next section measures what that test could find.

**A correction made during the analysis.** The first pass tested interactions on the raw scale and returned dozens of hits, nearly all from cells of five to nine lines. Checking the tail of the p-value distribution showed the tests were too liberal there: 2.6 times the expected number of p < 0.001 for genes in the smallest cells, and 27 times for drug effects inside the smallest contexts. Selective dependencies and drug responses are heavy-tailed, so one extreme line can carry a small cell. The screen was rerun on rank-normalised outcomes, which restored calibration (Figure 5b), and the hits disappeared. Effect sizes are still reported on the raw scale.

# What the cancer-type tests could detect

```{r fig9}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig9_power_clean_shift.png")
```

The context screens found nothing beyond chance. This section asks what they could have found, had Y loss created a dependency in one cancer type only. Cancer type is taken at three levels of the Oncotree hierarchy: lineage, primary disease and subtype.

The limits come from the screen's own model, not from a formula. A real selective gene is shifted towards more dependent in the Y-negative lines of one cancer type and tested as the one gene added to the real ones. It counts as found when its p-value is below a bar, and three bars are used. "Named in advance" is one gene chosen beforehand, at p < 0.05. "Alone" is the cancer type analysed on its own, genome-wide over its `r num(power$selective_genes)` selective genes: the p-value at which one more test would pass FDR 0.05 in that family. "As run" is the screen's rule, which needs the interaction and the effect inside the cancer type, each among all cancer types of that level. Each probability comes from `r power$simulation$benchmark_replicates` or `r power$simulation$shift_genes` simulated genes and so carries a Monte Carlo error of about 0.02; a count of cancer types at the 80% mark can move by one or two.

```{r census}
show(power_census[, .(Level = level_names[level], `Cancer types with lines` = with_lines, `Both Y groups present` = both_groups, `At least 5 lines per group` = at_least_5,
  `At least 10 per group` = at_least_10, `Lines in a testable type` = sprintf("%d of %d", lines_in_testable, lines_total))],
  caption = "Cancer types among the lines with CRISPR data and a Y call. Five lines per Y group is the gate the screen used.")
```

- **Many cancer types cannot be tested.** At least five Y-negative and five Y-positive lines exist for `r census_of("lineage")$at_least_5` of `r census_of("lineage")$with_lines` lineages, which hold `r census_of("lineage")$lines_in_testable` of the `r census_of("lineage")$lines_total` lines, but for only `r census_of("disease")$at_least_5` of `r census_of("disease")$with_lines` primary diseases and `r census_of("subtype")$at_least_5` of `r census_of("subtype")$with_lines` subtypes (Figure 9a, b). The screen tested every one of them. The largest it could not test are `r names_of(untestable[level == "lineage"][1:3])` among lineages, and `r names_of(untestable[level == "subtype"][1:6])` among subtypes.
- **A gene named in advance is a different matter.** At p < 0.05, a shift of `r r2(min(named_chronos$limit))` to `r r2(max(named_chronos$limit))` Chronos units (median `r r2(median(named_chronos$limit))`) is found 80% of the time in every one of the `r n_types` tested cancer types. The limits that follow are the price of searching the genome.
- **Genome-wide, the effect must be large.** With the cancer type analysed alone, the shift found 80% of the time runs from `r r2(largest_type$limit)` Chronos units in `r largest_type$label` to `r r2(smallest_reached$limit)` in `r smallest_reached$label` (Figure 9c). Among the cancer types that get there, the median is `r r2(median_limit("lineage"))` for lineages, `r r2(median_limit("disease"))` for primary diseases and `r r2(median_limit("subtype"))` for subtypes. Under the screen's own rule it runs from `r r2(min(run_reached$limit))` (`r run_reached[which.min(limit), label]`) to `r r2(max(run_reached$limit))` (`r run_reached[which.max(limit), label]`). For scale, the DDX3X effect is `r r2(genes[symbol == "DDX3X", estimate])` and the ZFX effect `r r2(genes[symbol == "ZFX", estimate])`, and the pan-cancer scan could find a shift of about `r r2(pan_limit)` by the normal-theory formula.
- **The smallest tested types have a ceiling.** In `r nrow(never_one)` of the `r n_types` tested cancer types no shift of any size is found 80% of the time, even with the type analysed alone: `r names_of(never_one)`. Under the screen's own rule that is true of `r nrow(never_run)`. The ceiling comes from the rank-based scores, which the screen had to use because the raw-scale test was miscalibrated in small cells. Five or six lines can only be so extreme in rank, and a larger shift does not help: from 6 to 10 SD, detection rises by `r r2(ceiling_rise)` at most. A test confined to the cancer type's own lines would do worse. For `r n_floor` of the tested types the smallest p-value an exact two-sample test can give is above the bar; the screen gets below it only because it ranks each line against all `r power$lines` and takes its variance from all genes.
- **The textbook formula is too optimistic.** By the normal-theory formula the limits would be `r r2(min(formula$best_case, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r r2(max(formula$best_case, na.rm = TRUE))` SD of a gene's line-to-line spread. The simulation agrees within `r round(100 * max(abs(formula_top$as_analysed / formula_top$best_case - 1), na.rm = TRUE))`% in the three largest cancer types, needs `r r2(median(formula$as_analysed / formula$best_case, na.rm = TRUE))` times as much in the median type that reaches 80% at all, and never gets there in `r nrow(never_one)`.

```{r limits}
limit_tab <- merge(one_chronos[, .(context_id, level, label, n_negative, n_positive, alone_80 = limit)], limit_of("one_type", "chronos", 0.5)[, .(context_id, alone_50 = limit)], by = "context_id")
limit_tab <- merge(limit_tab, run_chronos[, .(context_id, run_80 = limit)], by = "context_id")
limit_tab <- merge(limit_tab, one_sd[, .(context_id, alone_ceiling = ceiling)], by = "context_id")
limit_tab <- merge(limit_tab, run_sd[, .(context_id, run_ceiling = ceiling)], by = "context_id")
limit_tab <- merge(limit_tab, named_chronos[, .(context_id, named_80 = limit)], by = "context_id")
limit_tab <- limit_tab[order(-harmonic(n_negative, n_positive))]
cell <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "not reached", r2(x))
limit_table <- function(l, first = FALSE) {
  note <- if (first) " Smallest clean shift, in Chronos units. Named gene: found 80% of the time for one gene named in advance. 50% and 80%: found that often with the cancer type analysed alone. As run: found 80% of the time under the screen's rule. Lines: Y-negative / Y-positive. Ceiling: probability of finding a shift of 10 SD. 'Not reached': no shift up to 2 Chronos units is found that often." else " Columns as in the table of lineages."
  show(limit_tab[level == l, .(`Cancer type` = label, Lines = sprintf("%d\u00a0/\u00a0%d", n_negative, n_positive), `Named gene` = cell(named_80), `50%` = cell(alone_50), `80%` = cell(alone_80), `80%, as run` = cell(run_80),
    Ceiling = r2(alone_ceiling), `Ceiling, as run` = r2(run_ceiling))], caption = paste0(c(lineage = "Lineages.", disease = "Primary diseases.", subtype = "Subtypes.")[[l]], note))
}
limit_table("lineage", first = TRUE)
```

```{r limits-disease}
limit_table("disease")
```

```{r limits-subtype}
limit_table("subtype")
```

```{r fig10}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig10_power_benchmarks.png")
```

Known vulnerabilities give the scale. Each was estimated in the same eligible male lines with the same model. It was then moved: a resampled copy of the benchmark gene, with its own noise and lineage levels, in which the dependent lines are the Y-negative lines of one cancer type.

```{r benchmarks}
bench_tab <- reach_own[order(match(class, unique(power_bench$class)), -abs(effect))]
bench_tab <- merge(bench_tab, power_bench[, .(benchmark = label, sd_altered, sd_reference)], by = "benchmark", sort = FALSE)
bench_tab <- merge(bench_tab, reach_typical[, .(benchmark, ordinary = types)], by = "benchmark", sort = FALSE)
class_sizes <- bench_tab[, .N, by = class]
show(bench_tab[, .(Benchmark = benchmark, Effect = r2(effect), Spread = sprintf("%s / %s", r2(sd_altered), r2(sd_reference)), `80%` = types, `50%` = half, `80%, as run` = as_run, Best = r2(best), `80%, ordinary gene` = ordinary)],
  caption = sprintf("Known vulnerabilities and the number of tested cancer types (of %d) in which the screen would find a Y-loss effect like them. Effect in Chronos units; spread is the SD among altered and among other lines. 80%% and 50%%: cancer types finding a copy of the benchmark gene that often when analysed alone; as run: under the screen's rule; best: the highest probability in any cancer type. Last column: the same effect and spread on an ordinary selective gene. Rows are in the classes of Figure 10a: %s.",
    n_types, paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", class_sizes$class, class_sizes$N), collapse = ", ")))
```

- **The strongest oncogene addictions would have been called in the larger cancer types.** Under the screen's own rule, a Y-loss effect like BRAF dependency in BRAF V600E lines would have been called in `r called("BRAF in BRAF V600E")` of the `r n_types` tested cancer types, one like NRAS in NRAS Q61 in `r called("NRAS in NRAS Q61")`, KRAS in KRAS-driver lines in `r called("KRAS in KRAS-driver")` and CTNNB1 in APC loss in `r called("CTNNB1 in APC loss")`; the other `r sum(reach_own$as_run == 0)` of `r nrow(reach_own)` benchmarks in none. The screen made `r if (cancer_calls == 0) "no call" else sprintf("%d calls", cancer_calls)` in any cancer type, so for those cancer types its silence is informative: Y loss creates no dependency of that size and shape there. With the cancer type analysed alone the four counts rise to `r types_finding("BRAF in BRAF V600E")`, `r types_finding("NRAS in NRAS Q61")`, `r types_finding("KRAS in KRAS-driver")` and `r types_finding("CTNNB1 in APC loss")` (Figure 10a), and `r reach_own[types > 0, .N]` of `r nrow(reach_own)` benchmarks are found in at least one cancer type.
- **Analysed alone, the real data are almost as quiet.** At that bar the four established dependencies pass in `r power_alone[established == TRUE, .N]` gene-by-type combinations, and `r nrow(alone_other)` other `r if (nrow(alone_other) == 1) "combination does" else "combinations do"`: `r paste(sprintf("%s in %s (effect %s, FDR %s within that cancer type and %s among all of its level, %d vs %d lines)", alone_other$symbol, alone_other$label, r2(alone_other$inside), f3(alone_other$own_fdr), f3(alone_other$inside_fdr_class), alone_other$n_negative, alone_other$n_positive), collapse = "; ")`. With `r n_types` cancer types each searched on its own, one or two passes of this kind are expected by chance, so this is a lead and not a finding.
- **Smaller effects would not.** `r reach_own[types == 0, .N]` of `r nrow(reach_own)` benchmarks are found 80% of the time in no cancer type, even analysed alone. Among them are WRN in MSI lines (`r r2(best_of("WRN in MSI"))` at best), SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-mutant lines (`r r2(best_of("SMARCA2 in SMARCA4-mutant"))`) and PRMT5 in MTAP-deleted lines (`r r2(best_of("PRMT5 in MTAP-deleted"))`).
- **Where the gene is already a dependency, there is no room.** A copy of a benchmark gene is hardest to find in the lineage that already depends on it: BRAF in skin (`r r2(bench_at(detect_own, "BRAF in BRAF V600E", "Skin"))`, where BRAF sits `r r2(abs(level_of("BRAF in BRAF V600E", "Skin")))` Chronos units below the typical line even without V600E), KRAS in bowel (`r r2(bench_at(detect_own, "KRAS in KRAS-driver", "Bowel"))`) and CTNNB1 in bowel and liver (`r r2(bench_at(detect_own, "CTNNB1 in APC loss", "Bowel"))` and `r r2(bench_at(detect_own, "CTNNB1 in APC loss", "Liver"))`). Lines already at the bottom of the ranking move little in rank when pushed further. Across the `r nrow(room)` benchmarks whose detection varies by lineage, the rank correlation between the gene's level in a lineage and detection there has a median of `r r2(median(room$rho, na.rm = TRUE))`.
- **The gene matters as well as the effect.** Benchmark genes are noisier than most. With the same mean effect and spread put on an ordinary selective gene, `r sum(reach_typical$types > 0)` of `r nrow(reach_typical)` benchmarks reach 80% in at least one cancer type, against `r sum(reach_own$types > 0)` as copies of themselves. EIF1AX shows the gap: an effect of its size on an ordinary gene would be found in `r reach_typical[benchmark == "EIF1AX in Y-negative", types]` of `r n_types` cancer types, and EIF1AX itself in `r types_finding("EIF1AX in Y-negative")`. A Y-loss dependency in a quiet gene is easier to see than these benchmarks suggest; one in a gene as variable as they are is not. Either way the synthetic-lethal and collateral benchmarks other than STAG1 stay out of reach: on an ordinary gene WRN, SMARCA2, ARID1B, CREBBP, PIK3CB, PRMT5 and MAT2A reach 80% in `r if (weak_best == 0) "no cancer type" else sprintf("at most %d cancer types", weak_best)`.
- **Chance alone gives nothing.** A copy of each benchmark gene with no effect passes the genome-wide bar in at most `r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * max(power_null$one_type))`% of runs, and real genes with no shift in `r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * power$null_shift$one_type)`% at most.
- **The four established dependencies as a check.** Inside single lineages DDX3X, EIF1AX, ZFX and RPS4X reach genome-wide significance in `r paste(positive_lineage$alone, collapse = ", ")` of `r positive_by_level[level == "lineage", types]` lineages (Figure 10b). These effects sit in every Y-negative line, not in one cancer type, so for this comparison the genes were resampled that way: the simulation then expects `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", positive_lineage$everywhere), collapse = ", ")`, that is `r sprintf("%.1f", positive_expected)` recoveries against `r positive_seen` seen. A count that high has probability `r r2(ppois(positive_seen - 1, positive_expected, lower.tail = FALSE))` under the simulation, so the two agree, and the simulation does not flatter the argument: if anything it finds a little less than the data did. (With the effect confined to the one lineage, as for the benchmarks, it expects `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", positive_lineage$predicted), collapse = ", ")`.) None of the four is recovered in `r positive_by_level[level == "lineage", none]` of the `r positive_by_level[level == "lineage", types]` lineages. Among primary diseases `r positive_by_level[level == "disease", alone]` of `r positive_by_level[level == "disease", chances]` gene-by-type combinations are recovered, and among subtypes `r positive_by_level[level == "subtype", alone]` of `r positive_by_level[level == "subtype", chances]`. Effects that are real, and among the largest in the genome, are mostly invisible one cancer type at a time.
- **Genotype-defined contexts.** The same simulation on the `r nrow(genotype_one)` driver, copy-number, molecular-subtype and genome-doubling or MSI contexts gives an 80% limit below 2 Chronos units in `r sum(genotype_one$reachable)` of them, with a median of `r r2(median(genotype_one$limit_chronos, na.rm = TRUE))`; in `r sum(!genotype_one$inside_fitted)` the screen could not fit the effect inside the context at all. Inside such a context the Y effect is estimated within lineage, so what counts is how many lineages hold both Y groups, not how many lines there are. `r genotype_example$label` amplification has `r genotype_example$n_neg_in` Y-negative and `r genotype_example$n_pos_in` Y-positive lines, but only `r genotype_example$lineages_with_both` of its `r genotype_example$lineages` lineages hold both, and a shift of 2 Chronos units is found `r round(100 * genotype_example$detection_at_largest_shift)`% of the time. The large contexts do better than any cancer type: TP53 alteration and genome doubling reach 80% at `r r2(genotype_one[label == "TP53" & class == "driver", limit_chronos])` and `r r2(genotype_one[label == "WGD", limit_chronos])`.
- **Drugs.** By the normal-theory formula, which is the best case, a lineage needs an effect of `r r2(min(drug_testable$best_case_dataset_sd, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r r2(max(drug_testable$best_case_dataset_sd, na.rm = TRUE))` SD to be the one discovery among a dataset's compounds. BRAF-inhibitor response in BRAF-altered lines, the drug benchmark of the pipeline controls, is `r r2(min(drug_by_dataset$braf, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r r2(max(drug_by_dataset$braf, na.rm = TRUE))` SD; an effect of that size would be found in `r sum(drug_by_dataset$would_find_braf)` of `r sum(drug_by_dataset[!is.na(braf), lineages])` dataset-by-lineage tests.

**What this means for the choice of experiment.** The cancer-type nulls in this analysis are bounded, not empty. In the best-covered cancer types a Y-loss dependency as strong as the strongest oncogene addictions (`r paste(strongest, collapse = ", ")`) would have been called. One the size of a known synthetic-lethal or collateral dependency would not have been, STAG1 in STAG2-mutant lines apart, and most primary diseases and subtypes could not be asked at all. Two of the reasons belong to the cell-line panel, and no reanalysis changes them:

- **Fixed sample sizes.** The number of Y-negative lines per cancer type is what it is: `r census_of("lineage")$with_lines - census_of("lineage")$at_least_5` of `r census_of("lineage")$with_lines` lineages, `r census_of("disease")$with_lines - census_of("disease")$at_least_5` of `r census_of("disease")$with_lines` primary diseases and `r census_of("subtype")$with_lines - census_of("subtype")$at_least_5` of `r census_of("subtype")$with_lines` subtypes cannot be tested.
- **Association.** A difference that is found is still a difference between groups of unrelated lines, which also differ in TP53 status, genome doubling and subtype.

Two more belong to the analysis, and no better one is at hand:

- **A ceiling in the small types.** In `r nrow(never_run)` of the `r n_types` that can be tested, the screen's rule finds no effect of any size 80% of the time. The rank-based scores cause it, and the raw-scale test that would avoid it was miscalibrated in exactly those cells.
- **Dilution.** The test is of a group mean. A dependency present in only some Y-negative lines of a cancer type is spread across all of them, which is one reason the benchmarks do worse than clean shifts of the same size; the benchmark genes' own noise is another.

An isogenic comparison, the same line with and without the Y chromosome, sets its own sample size, can be made in a cancer type that has no usable lines here, and attributes a difference to Y loss itself. This analysis does not measure how sensitive such a screen would be, and one background does not generalise to others.

# Organoids, RNAi and primary AML

```{r fig11}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig11_more_models.png")
```

The cell lines are too few per cancer type, so three public sources were screened for vulnerabilities that go with Y loss: Sanger organoid CRISPR screens (Herranz-Ors et al. 2026), RNAi (DEMETER2) on the cell lines, and drug response of primary AML samples (BeatAML2). The design was written down before any of their results was read; the two later changes are marked where they apply.

```{r ext-overview}
ext_overview <- rbind(
  data.table(Screen = "Organoids, all types", Models = ext_pair(sum(ext_org_primary$y_negative == 1), sum(ext_org_primary$y_negative == 0)), Tests = num(nrow(ext_org_pan)),
    Passing = ext_list(ext_org_hits$symbol), Shuffled = ext_shuffled(ext_org_cal, "pan_fdr_hits")),
  data.table(Screen = "Organoids, by type", Models = ext_pair(ext_count("Colorectal", 1) + ext_count("Oesophageal", 1), ext_count("Colorectal", 0) + ext_count("Oesophageal", 0)), Tests = num(ext_org_scan$type_tests),
    Passing = ext_count_word(ext_org_scan$type_specific + ext_org_scan$inside_only), Shuffled = ext_shuffled(ext_org_cal, "inside_fdr_hits")),
  data.table(Screen = "RNAi, by context", Models = ext_pair(ext_rnai$y_negative, ext_rnai$y_positive), Tests = num(ext_rnai$screen_tests),
    Passing = ext_count_word(ext_rnai$screen_context_specific), Shuffled = ext_shuffled(ext_rnai_cal, "specific")),
  data.table(Screen = "Cell lines + organoids, all types", Models = ext_pair(ext_pw("Pan-cancer", "Combined")$n_negative, ext_pw("Pan-cancer", "Combined")$n_positive), Tests = num(nrow(ext_pan)),
    Passing = ext_list(ext_pan_hits$symbol), Shuffled = "not run"),
  data.table(Screen = "Cell lines + organoids, by type", Models = ext_pair(ext_pw(ext_col, "Combined")$n_negative + ext_pw(ext_oes, "Combined")$n_negative, ext_pw(ext_col, "Combined")$n_positive + ext_pw(ext_oes, "Combined")$n_positive),
    Tests = num(nrow(ext_within)), Passing = ext_count_word(sum(ext_within$combined_hit)), Shuffled = "not run"),
  data.table(Screen = "Primary AML, inhibitors", Models = ext_pair(nrow(ext_aml_high), ext_aml_screen[f == 0, .N]), Tests = num(nrow(ext_aml_drugs)),
    Passing = ext_list(ext_drug(ext_aml_hits$inhibitor)), Shuffled = ext_shuffled(ext_aml_cal, "fdr_hits"))
)
show(ext_overview, col.names = c("Screen", "Models", "Tests", "Passing", "Shuffled"), align = "lllll",
  caption = "The added screens. Models: Y-negative / Y-positive (AML: Y-loss fraction of at least 0.5 / of 0 in the cohort). Shuffled: passing in each of five runs with Y status shuffled.")
```

## Organoids

- **Y status.** Of `r ext_org$screened` screened organoids, `r ext_org$males` are male by both clinical record and genome. The cell-line rule was applied on the organoids' own RNA scale and checked against chrY copy number (Figure 11b). RNA and DNA agree in `r ext_tier("concordant")`; `r ext_tier("rna_led_dna_ambiguous")` have a definite RNA call and an unclear DNA result, and keep the RNA call; `r ext_tier("rna_intermediate")` have intermediate RNA and `r ext_tier("discordant")` is contradicted by DNA, and these `r ext_tier(c("rna_intermediate", "discordant"))` are set aside. Of the RNA-led calls, `r ext_org_kept_dna` are Y-negative organoids that express no Y gene but keep most of the male-specific region in DNA (the red points at the right of Figure 11b), and `r ext_org_low_dna` are Y-positive organoids that express all seven Y genes with little chrY left in DNA, as a minority of cells keeping the Y would give. The DNA-confirmed definition among the follow-up checks leaves all RNA-led calls out. Without the `r ext_org$males - ext_org$eligible` adenoma and with one organoid per patient, `r nrow(ext_org_primary)` remain: `r ext_count("Colorectal", 1)` Y-negative and `r ext_count("Colorectal", 0)` Y-positive colorectal, `r ext_count("Oesophageal", 1)` and `r ext_count("Oesophageal", 0)` oesophageal, and `r ext_org_primary[!OncotreeLineage %in% c("Colorectal", "Oesophageal"), .N]` of other types (Figure 11a). No organoid or donor identifier appears in the DepMap model table.
- **Two genes pass, and both were expected.** `r ext_list(sprintf("%s (%s, FDR %s)", ext_org_hits$symbol, r2(ext_org_hits$estimate_chronos_equivalent), pv(ext_org_hits$fdr)))` are more needed in Y-negative organoids (Figure 11c). Effects are in Chronos-equivalent units: the organoid score divided by `r r2(ext_org$effect_scale)`, the typical depletion of a common-essential gene in these screens. No other gene of `r num(nrow(ext_org_pan))` passes; the next is `r ext_org_next$symbol` (FDR `r r2(ext_org_next$fdr)`). The same scan with Y level as a continuous score, over `r ext_org_scan$continuous_organoids` male organoids with the intermediate ones included, gives `r if (setequal(ext_org_continuous$symbol, ext_org_hits$symbol)) "the same genes" else ext_list(ext_org_continuous$symbol)` (FDR `r pv(max(ext_org_continuous$fdr))`). Both hits were visible in an undocumented comparison already on disk, so they count as replication in independent models, not as discoveries.
- **Both hold in every follow-up check.** Each keeps the label `r unique(ext_org_hits$label)`. Each keeps its sign under `r ext_org_definitions` other Y-status definitions (among them RNA and DNA in agreement, `r ext_org_checks[variant == "dna_confirmed", n[1]]` organoids), in microsatellite-stable organoids only, with the other library, with both organoids of a patient, with two further covariate sets and with any one organoid left out; the largest p across these is `r pv(ext_org_checks[!check %like% "permutation", max(p, na.rm = TRUE)])`. The permutation p is `r pv(max(ext_org_permutation$p))`, the smallest that 20,000 shuffles can give.
- **ZFX does not carry over, and EIF1AX cannot be tested.** ZFX has an effect of `r r2(ext_g("ZFX")$estimate_chronos_equivalent)` in organoids (p = `r pv(ext_g("ZFX")$p)`) against `r r2(genes[symbol == "ZFX", estimate])` in cell lines, and the two sources differ (p = `r pv(ext_pan[symbol == "ZFX", smd_difference_p])`; the organoid effect is near zero on any scale). EIF1AX is not in the organoid gene set. CORO1A, the third gene of the comparison on disk, does not pass here (FDR `r r2(ext_g("CORO1A")$fdr)`) and has no support in cell lines (p = `r pv(ext_seen[symbol == "CORO1A", cell_p])`) or RNAi (p = `r pv(ext_seen[symbol == "CORO1A", rnai_p])`).
- **Nothing is specific to a cancer type.** Among `r num(ext_org$genes_selective)` selective genes tested in colorectal and oesophageal organoids, `r ext_count_word(ext_org_scan$type_specific)` `r if (ext_org_scan$type_specific == 1) "is" else "are"` specific to one type and `r ext_count_word(ext_org_scan$inside_only)` `r if (ext_org_scan$inside_only == 1) "passes" else "pass"` inside one type at FDR 0.05 (`r ext_shuffled(ext_org_cal, "inside_fdr_hits")` with Y status shuffled). The interaction with cancer type needs a larger effect than a test inside one type, so the inside tests are where a finding was possible. Taken as genes named in advance, DDX3X and RPS4X hold inside both types: p = `r pv(ext_in("DDX3X", "Colorectal")$inside_p)` and `r pv(ext_in("RPS4X", "Colorectal")$inside_p)` in colorectal, `r pv(ext_in("DDX3X", "Oesophageal")$inside_p)` and `r pv(ext_in("RPS4X", "Oesophageal")$inside_p)` in oesophageal organoids.
- **Nothing is specific to a genotype.** The secondary panel (`r ext_list(ext_panel)`) gives `r if (ext_org_scan$genotype_specific == 0) "no specific result" else sprintf("%d specific result%s", ext_org_scan$genotype_specific, if (ext_org_scan$genotype_specific == 1) "" else "s")` in `r num(ext_org_scan$genotype_tests)` tests. The `r nrow(ext_org_inside)` detections inside a group are the same two genes: `r ext_list(sprintf("%s in %s", ext_org_inside$symbol, ext_genotype_name(ext_org_inside$context)))` organoids.
- **Controls and calibration.** Known biology is recovered: KRAS is more needed in KRAS-mutant organoids (p = `r pv(ext_ctl("KRAS")$p)`), WRN in MSI organoids (p = `r pv(ext_ctl("WRN")$p)`), and MDM2 less in TP53-altered ones (p = `r pv(ext_ctl("MDM2")$p)`). The scan over all organoids has lambda `r r2(ext_org_scan$lambda)`, and shuffled Y status gives `r ext_shuffled(ext_org_cal, "pan_fdr_hits")` hits in five runs.
- **Screen quality and Y status.** Y-negative organoids have somewhat better screens: a median true-positive rate of `r r2(ext_org_primary[y_negative == 1, median(TPR)])` against `r r2(ext_org_primary[y_negative == 0, median(TPR)])` (rank-sum p = `r pv(ext_tpr_rank)`). With tumour type, library and MSI in the model the difference is `r r2(ext_tpr_fit[["Estimate"]])` (p = `r pv(ext_tpr_fit[["Pr(>|t|)"]])`). A better screen depletes every needed gene further, which would favour "more needed in Y-negative". The fits on the raw scale therefore weight each organoid by its noise, estimated without Y status in the model. A hit keeps its label only if it survives adjustment for the organoid's common-essential depletion and also shows in the depletion calls with screen quality in the model. Common-essential depletion itself does not differ between the Y groups (`r f3(ext_org_scan$essential_shift$estimate)`, p = `r pv(ext_org_scan$essential_shift$p)`).
- **A correction to the first run.** The first run also applied the weights to the rank-based tests and reported DDX3X as passing genome-wide inside colorectal organoids, and with it one combined result. Shuffled Y status then showed the weighted rank tests to be inflated. The weights were removed from every rank-based test, which now have lambda `r r2(ext_org_scan$inside_lambda)` (`r r2(min(ext_org_scan$shuffled_inside_lambda))` to `r r2(max(ext_org_scan$shuffled_inside_lambda))` with Y status shuffled), and both detections are withdrawn.

## RNAi

- **What to expect.** RNAi covers `r ext_rnai$lines` of the lines (`r ext_rnai$y_negative` Y-negative, `r ext_rnai$y_positive` Y-positive), about half the CRISPR cohort, and `r ext_rnai_shared` of them are CRISPR lines. The CRISPR context screen found nothing beyond chance, so a genome-wide finding here was unlikely, and agreement between the two assays is not independent replication.
- **Nothing context-specific.** The context screen was repeated on RNAi with `r num(ext_rnai$genes_screen)` selective genes and `r ext_rnai$contexts_fitted` contexts: `r num(ext_rnai$screen_tests)` tests, each kept only where every Y-by-context cell holds at least five lines with data for that gene. `r ext_start(ext_rnai$screen_context_specific)` context-specific, and `r ext_count_word(ext_rnai$focused_context_specific)` in the focus family of `r ext_rnai$genes_focused` X-linked genes (`r ext_shuffled(ext_rnai_cal, "specific")` with Y status shuffled).
- **Inside a context, only the paired genes.** Without an interaction, `r nrow(ext_rnai_inside)` tests pass inside a context (`r ext_shuffled(ext_rnai_cal, "inside")` with Y status shuffled): `r ext_list(sprintf("%s in %d", ext_rnai_by_gene$symbol, ext_rnai_by_gene$N))`, all in large genotype groups (`r ext_list(unique(ext_context_name(ext_rnai_inside$class, ext_rnai_inside$label)))`) and none in a cancer type. Within the focus family, `r ext_rnai_type_text`. These are the pan-cancer RNAi results for RPS4X and DDX3X seen again inside large groups.
- **Agreement with CRISPR is modest.** Over `r num(sum(ext_cross$pairs))` gene-by-context pairs tested in both assays, `r sum(ext_cross$inside_both_nominal)` are nominal (p < 0.05) in both with the same sign, and the rank correlation of the effects is `r r2(ext_cross[, weighted.mean(inside_rank_correlation, inside_tested)])`. Two assays that shared nothing would give about `r round(sum(ext_cross$inside_expected_by_chance))` such pairs, but these share most of their lines, so some agreement is expected with no Y effect at all, and the count is not evidence of one. Of `r nrow(ext_leads)` leads from the cell-line screens, `r sum(ext_leads$tested_in_rnai)` can be tested in RNAi and `r nrow(ext_leads_agree)` agree, all of them `r ext_list(unique(ext_leads_agree$symbol))`. The other `r sum(!ext_leads$tested_in_rnai)` cannot: EIF1AX is not in the RNAi data, and the `r nrow(ext_leads_other)` leads outside the paired genes, CIB1 in bladder among them, are not screened there or fall below the gate.

## Cell lines and organoids combined

Each source was screened alone and then combined per gene from its own p-value and sign, weighted by its design. The two sources score on different scales, so effect sizes are not pooled. RNAi is left out of the combination because most of its lines are the CRISPR lines.

- **All types together: the paired genes.** Over `r num(nrow(ext_pan))` genes in both scans, `r nrow(ext_pan_hits)` pass: `r ext_list(ext_both)`, supported by both sources, and `r ext_list(ext_one)`, carried by the cell lines alone (Figure 11d). In Chronos-equivalent units DDX3X is `r r2(ext_g("DDX3X")$estimate_chronos_equivalent)` in organoids against `r r2(genes[symbol == "DDX3X", estimate])` in cell lines, and RPS4X `r r2(ext_g("RPS4X")$estimate_chronos_equivalent)` against `r r2(genes[symbol == "RPS4X", estimate])`. The standardised effects differ for DDX3X (p = `r pv(ext_pan[symbol == "DDX3X", smd_difference_p])`) and not for RPS4X (p = `r pv(ext_pan[symbol == "RPS4X", smd_difference_p])`), but a noisier screen lowers a standardised effect, so that difference is not evidence of a weaker dependency. The organoids carry `r round(100 * ext_comb$organoid_weight_share)`% of the information, so this test gains little over the cell lines alone.
- **Inside a cancer type: no gene.** The Y effect inside colorectal cell lines was combined with that inside colorectal organoids, and oesophagogastric cell lines with oesophageal organoids, over `r num(ext_within[pair == ext_col, .N])` genes each. `r if (sum(ext_within$combined_hit) == 0) "No gene passes in either." else sprintf("%d pass.", sum(ext_within$combined_hit))` The closest are `r ext_best(ext_col)$symbol` in colorectal cancer (FDR `r r2(ext_best(ext_col)$combined_fdr)`) and `r ext_best(ext_oes)$symbol` in oesophagogastric cancer (FDR `r r2(ext_best(ext_oes)$combined_fdr)`) (Figure 11e). The organoids carry `r round(100 * ext_share(ext_col))`% and `r round(100 * ext_share(ext_oes))`% of the information.
- **MSI is in the colorectal model.** Microsatellite instability is more common among Y-positive models in both colorectal sources (`r ext_msi(0)` Y-positive against `r ext_msi(1)` Y-negative organoids), so an unadjusted combination would have rewarded any MSI-linked dependency, such as WRN. It is a covariate on both sides. Before it was added, the cell-line refit reproduced the stored p-values exactly.
