- **The oesophagogastric cell lines are mostly gastric.** All `r ext_oes_lines[OncotreeSubtype == "Esophageal Adenocarcinoma", .N]` oesophageal adenocarcinoma lines are Y-negative, so the `r ext_oes_lines[y_negative == 0, .N]` Y-positive lines of that group are gastric or junctional. All rectal lines are Y-negative as well.

## Primary AML

```{r fig12}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig12_primary_aml.png")
```

- **Y loss as a fraction.** A primary sample is a mixture of cells with and without the Y, so Y loss was measured as a fraction: the seven Y genes, each relative to its X partner and to the median male specimen. Below `r r2(ext_aml$floor)` the measure follows cell composition and is set to 0.
- **Who has Y loss.** With one specimen per patient there are `r nrow(ext_aml_all)` male patients, and the `r nrow(ext_aml_screen)` with a recorded age enter the drug screen. Of those, `r nrow(ext_aml_high)` have a fraction of at least 0.5: `r ext_aml_high[evidence_tier == "karyotype -Y", .N]` with a clone without Y in the karyotype, `r ext_aml_high[evidence_tier == "karyotype XY", .N]` with Y in every karyotyped cell and `r ext_aml_high[evidence_tier == "no karyotype", .N]` without a karyotype (Figure 12a). Where the karyotype gives a clone size, it tracks the RNA fraction (rank correlation `r r2(ext_aml$karyotype_rank_correlation)`, `r ext_aml$karyotype_compared` specimens; Figure 12b).
- **Control.** FLT3 inhibitors are more active in FLT3-ITD specimens, as known: `r ext_list(sprintf("%s (p = %s)", ext_drug(ext_aml_controls$inhibitor), pv(ext_aml_controls$p)))`.
- **One inhibitor passes, and it is less active with Y loss.** `r ext_short(ext_lead$inhibitor)`, a MEK inhibitor, loses activity as the Y-loss fraction rises: its rank-normalised AUC is `r r2(ext_lead$estimate)` SD higher at complete loss than at none (permutation p = `r pv(ext_lead$p)`, FDR `r f3(ext_lead$fdr)` among `r nrow(ext_aml_drugs)` inhibitors; Figure 12c). It was tested in `r ext_lead$n` patients, `r ext_lead$high_loss` of them with a fraction of at least 0.5. Shuffled Y loss gives `r ext_shuffled(ext_aml_cal, "fdr_hits")` hits in five runs. The other MEK inhibitors point the same way without passing, `r ext_list(sprintf("%s (p = %s)", ext_drug(ext_mek$inhibitor), pv(ext_mek$p)))`, and the MEK family as a whole does not pass (FDR `r r2(ext_mek_family$fdr)`); `r sum(ext_aml_families$fdr < 0.05)` of `r nrow(ext_aml_families)` drug families do.
- **No inhibitor is more active with Y loss.** The strongest result in that direction is `r ext_drug(ext_sensitive$inhibitor)` (FDR `r r2(ext_sensitive$fdr)`). Y loss does not go with a specimen's mean response across inhibitors either (p = `r pv(ext_aml_scan$general_response$p)`). The screen shows no drug vulnerability of AML with Y loss.
- **The hit passes the checks fixed in advance.** Its label is `r ext_lead$label`: it survives adjustment for TP53, FLT3-ITD, NPM1 and the specimen's mean response (p = `r pv(ext_lead$p_adjusted)`). With any one patient left out the largest p is `r pv(ext_fu("largest p")$p)`. The sign holds in all `r nrow(ext_aml_checks)` variants of exposure, specimens and covariates, among them Y loss confirmed by karyotype (p = `r pv(ext_fu("confirmed by karyotype")$p)`) and the Y genes alone (p = `r pv(ext_fu("Y genes alone")$p)`), and without the t(8;21) cases (p = `r pv(ext_lead$p_without_t8_21)`); the weakest is the variant "`r ext_aml_weakest$variant`" (p = `r pv(ext_aml_weakest$p)`, `r ext_aml_weakest$n` patients).
- **RAS-pathway mutations account for part of it.** This check was added after the hit was seen, because response to MEK inhibitors in AML follows mutations in NRAS, KRAS and PTPN11. No patient with Y loss and exome data carries one: `r ext_ras_high$ras_pathway_mutant` of `r ext_ras_high[, ras_pathway_mutant + ras_pathway_wild_type]` with a fraction of at least 0.5 and `r ext_ras_mid$ras_pathway_mutant` of `r ext_ras_mid[, ras_pathway_mutant + ras_pathway_wild_type]` with a smaller one, against `r ext_ras_none$ras_pathway_mutant` of `r ext_ras_none[, ras_pathway_mutant + ras_pathway_wild_type]` without Y loss (p = `r pv(ext_aml_ras$fisher_p[1])` for the first group against the rest; Figure 12d). With RAS-pathway status in the model the slope falls from `r r2(ext_fu("^main")$estimate)` to `r r2(ext_fu("plus RAS-pathway mutation")$estimate)` SD (p = `r pv(ext_fu("plus RAS-pathway mutation")$p)`), and among RAS-wild-type patients it is `r r2(ext_fu("wild-type specimens only")$estimate)` SD (p = `r pv(ext_fu("wild-type specimens only")$p)`). Neither would pass the screen. Part of the association is that Y loss marks RAS-wild-type disease.
- **Cell lines cannot check it.** `r ext_short(ext_lead$inhibitor)` was not screened as a single agent in the cell-line datasets. Across the `r ext_aml_compare$inhibitors[1]` inhibitors screened in both, the slopes do not agree in sign with the pan-cancer cell-line estimates (`r round(100 * ext_aml_compare$sign_agreement[1])`% agree, p = `r pv(ext_aml_compare$p[1])`). They agree in `r round(100 * ext_aml_compare$sign_agreement[2])`% of `r ext_aml_compare$inhibitors[2]` with the estimates inside myeloid lines (p = `r pv(ext_aml_compare$p[2])`, one of two tests).
- **Only large effects are detectable.** With at most `r nrow(ext_aml_high)` patients carrying the signal, and `r median(ext_aml_drugs$high_loss)` for the typical inhibitor, the screen finds `r r2(ext_aml_power$named)` SD for a named inhibitor and `r r2(ext_aml_power$genome_wide)` SD across the panel, at best.

## What the additions show

```{r ext-power}
ext_power_tab <- rbind(ext_power, ext_aml_power, fill = TRUE)[, .(
  Test = sub("^Pan-cancer$", "All cancer types", sub(" adenocarcinoma$", "", sub(", drug response$", "", analysis))), Source = sub(" \\(.*$", "", source),
  Models = ext_pair(n_negative, n_positive), `Named gene` = r2(named), `Genome-wide` = r2(genome_wide))]
show(ext_power_tab, align = "lllll",
  caption = "Best-case effect found 80% of the time, in SD of a gene's or inhibitor's spread between models, from each fitted design. Models: Y-negative / Y-positive; for BeatAML2, patients with a Y-loss fraction of at least 0.5 / of 0 in the cohort, the limit is that of the typical inhibitor, and the effect is that of complete loss. Named gene: one test at p < 0.05. Genome-wide: one more discovery in the family as tested. RNAi: a gene with data in every line.")
```

- **Two of the four paired genes hold in independent models.** DDX3X and RPS4X are more needed in Y-negative organoids. ZFX is not, and EIF1AX could not be tested.
- **More models did not produce a cancer-type-specific vulnerability.** With the organoids, the effect detectable genome-wide falls from `r r2(ext_pw(ext_col, "Cell lines")$genome_wide)` to `r r2(ext_pw(ext_col, "Combined")$genome_wide)` SD in colorectal and from `r r2(ext_pw(ext_oes, "Cell lines")$genome_wide)` to `r r2(ext_pw(ext_oes, "Combined")$genome_wide)` SD in oesophagogastric cancer, about what `r tolower(ext_lung$label)`, the largest lineage, reaches in the cell lines alone (`r r2(ext_lung$limit)` SD by simulation). No gene passes at that depth. These are best-case figures: a smaller effect would still be missed, and every other cancer type stays where the power analysis left it. For all cancer types together the organoids add little (`r r2(ext_pw("Pan-cancer", "Cell lines")$genome_wide)` to `r r2(ext_pw("Pan-cancer", "Combined")$genome_wide)` SD).
- **Primary samples add one lead, and it is not a vulnerability.** `r ext_short(ext_lead$inhibitor)` is less active with Y loss in AML. The result rests on `r ext_lead$high_loss` patients with a fraction of at least 0.5 among `r ext_lead$n` tested and is partly explained by RAS status. It is the one new result of six screens, each controlled on its own.

# DepMap NextGen models

```{r fig13}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig13_nextgen.png")
```

DepMap NextGen (Neiswender et al. 2026) has `r ng_prep$screened` organoid and neurosphere models with a screen that passed quality control, all with one Cas12a library and scored with Chronos, as the cell lines are. It was added on 2026-10-05 as a third CRISPR source: screened alone, then combined with the cell lines and the Sanger organoids. The four paired genes were named in advance, so for them NextGen is replication in independent models. Any other gene is a discovery, and in NextGen alone it must also clear a bar set by shuffling Y status. The cohort, the Y calls and the list of tests were frozen before any NextGen gene was compared with Y status. Two checks were added after results were seen; each is marked where it applies, and both can only weaken a result.

```{r ng-overview}
ng_overview <- rbind(
  data.table(Screen = "NextGen, the four paired genes", Models = ng_models(ng_primary), Tests = num(nrow(ng_paired)),
    Passing = if (length(ng_unconfirmed) == 0) ext_list(ng_confirmed) else sprintf("%s; %s on the model's p-value only", ext_list(ng_confirmed), ext_list(ng_unconfirmed)), Shuffled = ng_shuffled(sum(ng_null$named_replicated > 0))),
  data.table(Screen = "NextGen, all genes", Models = ng_models(ng_primary), Tests = num(nrow(ng_pan)),
    Passing = sprintf("%s; %s pass FDR and not the bar", ext_list(ng_pan[associated == TRUE & named == TRUE, symbol]), ext_list(ng_other$symbol)), Shuffled = ng_shuffled(sum(ng_null$pan_fdr_hits > 0))),
  data.table(Screen = "NextGen, inside oesophagus/stomach", Models = ng_models(ng_stomach), Tests = num(ng_scan$type_tests),
    Passing = ext_count_word(ng_scan$type_specific + ng_scan$inside_only), Shuffled = ng_shuffled(sum(ng_null$inside_fdr_hits > 0))),
  data.table(Screen = "Three sources, all types", Models = ext_pair(ng_pw("All cancer types", "Three sources")$n_negative, ng_pw("All cancer types", "Three sources")$n_positive), Tests = num(nrow(ng_three)),
    Passing = sprintf("%s; %s with small effects that do not hold up", ext_list(ng_three_hits[symbol %in% ng_names, symbol]), ext_list(ng_extra$symbol)), Shuffled = "not run"),
  data.table(Screen = "Three sources, inside oesophagogastric", Models = ext_pair(ng_pw(ng_oes, "Three sources")$n_negative, ng_pw(ng_oes, "Three sources")$n_positive), Tests = num(nrow(ng_oes_rows)),
    Passing = ext_count_word(sum(ng_oes_rows$combined_hit)), Shuffled = "not run"),
  data.table(Screen = "Pancreas pooled, the four paired genes", Models = ext_pair(ng_pn(ng_names[1])$n_negative, ng_pn(ng_names[1])$n_positive), Tests = num(nrow(ng_paired)),
    Passing = ext_list(ng_pool_holds), Shuffled = "exact test")
)
show(ng_overview, col.names = c("Screen", "Models", "Tests", "Passing", "Shuffled"), align = "lllll",
  caption = sprintf("The NextGen screens. Models: Y-negative / Y-positive. Shuffled: runs out of %d with Y status shuffled within stratum that gave at least one passing gene (for all genes, at FDR 0.05 before the bar).", ng_runs))
```

## The NextGen cohort

- **Y status.** Sex is the recorded sex: `r sum(ng_cohort$Sex == "Male")` of the screened models are male, `r sum(ng_cohort$Sex == "Female")` female and `r sum(ng_cohort$Sex == "Unknown")` unknown. The cell-line rule was applied on NextGen's own RNA scale and checked against the copy number of the seven Y genes (Figure 13b). One change was needed. Recorded females show almost no Y signal in this table: their largest mean over the seven genes is `r f3(ng_prep$rna_thresholds$female_mean_max)` log2 units, against `r r2(js("call_thresholds")$female_mean_max)` in the cell lines. "No Y expression" was therefore defined as at most the female maximum or `r 100 * ng_prep$rna_thresholds$ceiling_fraction`% of the typical male level, whichever is larger. Without that, males with a trace of Y signal and little or no chrY in DNA would have been left out. Across the `r nrow(ng_all_males)` recorded males in the data set, screened or not, RNA and DNA agree in `r ng_all_males[y_tier == "concordant", .N]` and contradict each other in `r ng_all_males[y_tier == "discordant", .N]`.
- **Who enters.** Of the `r nrow(ng_males)` screened males, `r ng_males[malignant == FALSE, .N]` are not cancers and `r ng_males[malignant == TRUE & shared_with_sanger == TRUE, .N]` come from donors that Sanger also screened; those donors stay with the Sanger cohort, as decided beforehand. A further `r ng_tier("rna_intermediate")` have intermediate RNA and are set aside, and `r ng_eligible[called == TRUE & first_of_donor == FALSE, .N]` are a second model of a donor already in the cohort; one of these pairs has unrelated names and was found by genotype alone (`r r2(ng_genotype_pair$genotype_similarity)` of rare damaging calls shared, where pairs below the cut share at most `r r2(ng_prep$genotype$other_max_below_cut)`). That leaves `r nrow(ng_primary)` models: `r ng_n(ng_primary, 1)` Y-negative and `r ng_n(ng_primary, 0)` Y-positive (Figure 13a). RNA and DNA agree for `r ng_tier("concordant")` of the `r nrow(ng_eligible)` eligible males; `r ng_tier("rna_led_dna_ambiguous")` keep an RNA call where DNA is unclear, and `r ng_tier("dna_only")` has DNA only.
- **Y status is tied to screen format and cancer type.** Of the `r ng_n(ng_primary, 1)` Y-negative models, `r ng_n(ng_dome, 1)` were screened as three-dimensional organoids, against `r ng_n(ng_dome, 0)` of the `r ng_n(ng_primary, 0)` Y-positive ones. Brain models, screened as neurospheres, are mostly Y-positive (`r ng_n(ng_brain, 1)` Y-negative, `r ng_n(ng_brain, 0)` Y-positive). The model therefore has one term per lineage and screen format. The `r ng_prep$design$models_in_one_group_strata` models in a stratum with one Y group add nothing, and the design is worth about `r round(ng_prep$design$balanced_equivalent)` balanced models per group.
- **Y loss travels with genome doubling and with noisier screens.** Genome doubling is found in `r ng_primary[y_negative == 1, sum(WGD == 1, na.rm = TRUE)]` of `r ng_primary[y_negative == 1, sum(!is.na(WGD))]` Y-negative models with a value, against `r ng_primary[y_negative == 0, sum(WGD == 1, na.rm = TRUE)]` of `r ng_primary[y_negative == 0, sum(!is.na(WGD))]` Y-positive ones. Median NNMD, a screen-quality score where more negative is better, is `r r2(ng_primary[y_negative == 1, median(ScreenNNMD)])` in Y-negative against `r r2(ng_primary[y_negative == 0, median(ScreenNNMD)])` in Y-positive models; within strata the difference is `r r2(ng_scan$quality_shift$estimate)` (p = `r pv(ng_scan$quality_shift$permutation_p)` from 20,000 shuffles). Fits on the Chronos scale weight each model by its noise, estimated without Y status in the model, and every hit is refitted with NNMD as a covariate. The per-model mean of the common-essential genes does not differ significantly between the groups (`r f3(ng_scan$essential_shift$estimate)`, p = `r pv(ng_scan$essential_shift$permutation_p)`), but gene by gene they lean the way a noisier screen would, as the scan below shows.

## NextGen alone

- **Controls.** Known biology is recovered in the `r sum(ng_cohort$malignant)` screened cancer models of both sexes: KRAS is more needed in models with a KRAS hotspot mutation (p = `r pv(ng_controls[gene == "KRAS", p])`; `r f3(ng_controls[gene == "KRAS", p_unweighted])` without the weights, which misses the gate of `r ng_controls[gene == "KRAS", p_max]`), and MDM2 less in TP53-altered ones (p = `r pv(ng_controls[gene == "MDM2", p])`).
- **Three of the four paired genes replicate; ZFX is not confirmed.** The rule set in advance asks for the cell-line sign and BH below 0.05 among the four. On the model's p-values all four pass it (Figure 13c and the table below). But the shuffles show that those p-values run small: with Y status shuffled, the rule called at least one paired gene replicated in `r sum(ng_null$named_replicated > 0)` of `r ng_runs` runs, about twice as often as well-calibrated p-values would. Each gene was therefore also given a permutation p-value from `r ng_num(ng_paired$permutation_shuffles[1])` shuffles, and the same rule was applied to those. This step was added after the first full run. With it, `r ext_list(ng_confirmed)` still replicate. ZFX is not confirmed: p = `r f3(ng_pg("ZFX")$p)` in the model and `r f3(ng_pg("ZFX")$permutation_p)` by permutation, and it is not significant with screen quality (p = `r f3(ng_fu("ZFX", "screen NNMD"))`) or with genome doubling, TP53 and aneuploidy in the model (p = `r f3(ng_fu("ZFX", "plus WGD"))`). Its sign holds in every variant. DDX3X is the strongest, at `r r2(ng_pg("DDX3X")$estimate)` Chronos units (p = `r pv(ng_pg("DDX3X")$p)`). It also passes genome-wide (FDR `r pv(ng_g("DDX3X")$fdr)`) and is the only one of the four to meet the robustness rule of the follow-up: with any one model left out its largest p is `r pv(ng_fu("DDX3X", "largest p"))`, and its estimate is `r r2(ng_fu("DDX3X", "dome organoids", "estimate"))` in the three-dimensional organoid screens alone and `r r2(ng_fu("DDX3X", "screen NNMD", "estimate"))` with screen quality in the model.

```{r ng-paired}
show(ng_paired[, .(Gene = symbol, `NextGen effect` = r2(estimate), `Model p` = pv(p), `Permutation p` = pv(permutation_p), `Rule on permutation p` = outcome_permutation, `Cell-line effect` = r2(cell_line_estimate),
  `Chance of replication` = ng_range(chance_at_strictest, chance_at_most_lenient))], align = "lllllll",
  caption = sprintf("The four paired genes in NextGen. Effects are Y-negative minus Y-positive, in Chronos units, here and in the cell-line scan. Permutation p: Y status shuffled within stratum, %s times. Rule on permutation p: the rule set in advance, applied to the permutation p-values; \"not replicated\" means not significant and significantly smaller than in the cell lines. Chance of replication: computed before the test from the cell-line effect, the design and each gene's spread, at the strictest and the most lenient BH step.", ng_num(ng_paired$permutation_shuffles[1])))
```

- **EIF1AX and ZFX show a smaller contrast here, and it comes from the Y-positive models.** EIF1AX is `r r2(ng_pg("EIF1AX")$estimate)` here against `r r2(ng_pg("EIF1AX")$cell_line_estimate)` in the cell lines (p = `r pv(ng_pg("EIF1AX")$difference_p)` for the difference), and ZFX `r r2(ng_pg("ZFX")$estimate)` against `r r2(ng_pg("ZFX")$cell_line_estimate)` (p = `r pv(ng_pg("ZFX")$difference_p)`). DDX3X and RPS4X do not differ (p = `r pv(ng_pg("DDX3X")$difference_p)` and `r pv(ng_pg("RPS4X")$difference_p)`). Both sources are scored in Chronos units, but with different libraries. Y-negative models score alike in the two sources (EIF1AX `r r2(ng_pg("EIF1AX")$mean_negative)` here and `r r2(ng_pg("EIF1AX")$cell_line_mean_negative)` in the cell lines; ZFX `r r2(ng_pg("ZFX")$mean_negative)` and `r r2(ng_pg("ZFX")$cell_line_mean_negative)`), while Y-positive models are more dependent here (EIF1AX `r r2(ng_pg("EIF1AX")$mean_positive)` against `r r2(ng_pg("EIF1AX")$cell_line_mean_positive)`; ZFX `r r2(ng_pg("ZFX")$mean_positive)` against `r r2(ng_pg("ZFX")$cell_line_mean_positive)`). A Cas12a guide that also cuts the Y copy would give exactly this pattern, as would another difference between the libraries or the cultures, and the collection has no guide map to check. The smaller contrast is therefore not evidence of a weaker dependency. It is also why the rule's "not replicated" for ZFX is reported as "not confirmed". RPS4X had the lowest chance of replication before the test, so a miss there would have been uninformative; it replicated.
- **No other gene is called.** Besides the four, `r nrow(ng_other)` genes pass FDR 0.05, `r ext_list(ng_other$symbol)`, both less needed in Y-negative models (`r r2(ng_other$estimate[1])` and `r r2(ng_other$estimate[2])` Chronos units). Neither clears the bar that `r ng_runs` shuffles set for a discovery, p < `r pv(ng_scan$null$pan_bar)`: `r ng_other$symbol[1]` misses it narrowly (p = `r formatC(ng_other$p[1], format = "e", digits = 2)`; the bar is itself an estimate from `r ng_runs` runs) and `r ng_other$symbol[2]` by more (p = `r pv(ng_other$p[2])`). Neither shows anything in the cell lines (`r f3(genes[symbol == ng_other$symbol[1], estimate])` and `r f3(genes[symbol == ng_other$symbol[2], estimate])` Chronos units; p = `r r2(genes[symbol == ng_other$symbol[1], p])` and `r r2(genes[symbol == ng_other$symbol[2], p])`), in the Sanger organoids or in RNAi, which all hold more models.
- **The scan's p-values run small, and screen quality is why.** Shuffled Y status alone gives a gene at FDR 0.05 in `r sum(ng_null$pan_fdr_hits > 0)` of `r ng_runs` runs (`r formatC(100 * mean(ng_null$pan_fdr_hits > 0), format = "f", digits = 1)`%), and `r r2(mean(ng_null$pan_below_1e5))` genes per run below p = `r ng_sci(1e-5)` where `r r2(1e-5 * nrow(ng_pan))` are expected, so an FDR hit in this scan is weak evidence by itself. The observed inflation factor is `r r2(ng_scan$lambda)`, a value that `r ng_scan$null$runs_at_or_above_lambda` of the `r ng_runs` shuffles reach. The excess sits in the `r num(ng_scan$essential$genes)` common-essential genes: their inflation factor is `r r2(ng_scan$essential$lambda)` against `r r2(ng_scan$essential$lambda_other_genes)` for the other genes, `r ng_pct(ng_scan$essential$positive)`% of their estimates are positive, and `r ng_scan$essential$runs_at_or_above_lambda` of the shuffles reach that. A noisier Y-negative screen gives this pattern, because every needed gene then looks a little less needed. With screen quality in the model the factor falls to `r r2(ng_scan$lambda_quality_adjusted)`. `r ng_other$symbol[1]` is one of the common-essential genes. Shuffling Y status also breaks its link with screen quality, so the bar from the shuffles does not protect against this bias; the quality-adjusted estimates do. The bias runs against the four paired genes, which are more needed in Y-negative models. The rank-based test inside oesophagus/stomach has an inflation factor of `r r2(ext_rr("nextgen_calibration")[run == "observed", inside_lambda])` (`r r2(ng_scan$null$inside_lambda_median)` at the median of the shuffles).
- **The cell-line label.** In the cell lines a hit is LOY-specific when it survives adjustment for genome doubling, TP53 and aneuploidy and for common-essential depletion, and also shows in the dependency calls; here it must survive screen quality as well. DDX3X survives the adjustments (`r r2(ng_g("DDX3X")$estimate_adjusted)` with the genomic covariates in `r ng_scan$adjusted_models` models, `r r2(ng_g("DDX3X")$estimate_quality_adjusted)` with screen quality). Its dependency calls point the same way, `r ng_pct(ng_g("DDX3X")$fraction_dependent_negative)`% of Y-negative against `r ng_pct(ng_g("DDX3X")$fraction_dependent_positive)`% of Y-positive models dependent, but the contrast is not significant with screen quality in the model (p = `r r2(ng_g("DDX3X")$dependent_fraction_p)`; `r f3(ng_g("DDX3X")$dependent_fraction_p_without_quality)` without it, which is how the cell-line stage tests it). `r if (ng_scan$loy_specific == 0) "No gene carries the label in NextGen alone" else sprintf("%d genes carry the label in NextGen alone", ng_scan$loy_specific)`; DDX3X is `r ng_g("DDX3X")$label` there.
- **Y level as a continuous score.** The same scan with the share of Y expression lost as a continuous score, over `r ng_scan$continuous_models` models with the intermediate ones included, gives `r ext_list(ng_continuous$symbol)` at FDR 0.05.
- **Nothing by cancer type.** Only oesophagus/stomach has five models per Y group (`r ng_n(ng_stomach, 1)` Y-negative, `r ng_n(ng_stomach, 0)` Y-positive). Among `r num(ng_scan$type_tests)` selective genes, `r ext_count_word(ng_scan$inside_only + ng_scan$type_specific)` passes inside it or is specific to it, and `r ext_count_word(sum(ng_null$inside_fdr_hits > 0))` of the `r ng_runs` shuffled runs gave a call. As a gene named in advance, DDX3X has p = `r pv(ng_types[symbol == "DDX3X", inside_p])` inside it.

## Three sources together

Each source enters with its own p-value and sign, weighted by its design, as in the two-source combination; a gene that one source does not test is combined over the others. The cell lines carry about `r ng_pct(ng_comb$weight_share$cell_lines)`% of the information, the Sanger organoids about `r ng_pct(ng_comb$weight_share$organoids)`% and NextGen about `r ng_pct(ng_comb$weight_share$nextgen)`%. No NextGen model is among the cell lines, and no donor is known to be shared between the sources.

- **The paired genes.** Over `r num(nrow(ng_three))` genes in the cell-line scan and at least one other, `r nrow(ng_three_hits)` pass, against `r sum(ng_three$two_source_hit, na.rm = TRUE)` with two sources. `r ext_list(ng_every)` are supported by every source that tests them. ZFX passes on the strength of the cell lines: the Sanger organoids show no ZFX effect, and NextGen alone does not confirm it, although under the one-sided rule of the combination NextGen counts as support (`r sub("supported by ", "", ng_t("ZFX")$evidence)`; Figure 13d). EIF1AX is new to the combined family. The Sanger library does not target it, so NextGen is its only test outside the cell lines.
- **Two more genes cross FDR 0.05, and neither is a vulnerability of Y loss.** `r ng_extra$symbol[1]` (FDR `r f3(ng_extra$combined_fdr[1])`) is less needed in Y-negative models in all three sources: `r r2(ng_extra$cell_estimate[1])` Chronos units in the cell lines (p = `r pv(ng_new$cell_p[1])`), `r r2(ng_extra$nextgen_estimate[1])` in NextGen (p = `r f3(ng_new$nextgen_p[1])`), and p = `r f3(ng_new$organoid_p[1])` in the Sanger organoids. In the cell lines it is a dependency in `r ng_pct(ng_extra$cell_dependent_negative[1])`% of Y-negative and `r ng_pct(ng_extra$cell_dependent_positive[1])`% of Y-positive lines. `r ng_extra$symbol[2]` (FDR `r f3(ng_extra$combined_fdr[2])`) has a slightly lower score in Y-negative models, `r r2(ng_extra$cell_estimate[2])` in the cell lines (p = `r pv(ng_new$cell_p[2])`) and `r r2(ng_extra$nextgen_estimate[2])` in NextGen (p = `r f3(ng_new$nextgen_p[2])`), with p = `r r2(ng_new$organoid_p[2])` in the organoids. But it is not a dependency: its mean score is above zero in both Y groups of both sources, and `r ng_dependent(ng_extra$symbol[2])[["cell"]]` of `r ng_dependent(ng_extra$symbol[2])[["cell_n"]]` cell lines and `r ng_dependent(ng_extra$symbol[2])[["nextgen"]]` of `r ng_dependent(ng_extra$symbol[2])[["nextgen_n"]]` NextGen models are called dependent on it. Neither gene is a hit in any single source, and in the cell lines both shifts are smaller than the 0.10 Chronos units that a single-source hit must reach; DDX3X is `r round(abs(ng_t("DDX3X")$cell_estimate / ng_extra$cell_estimate[1]))` times larger than `r ng_extra$symbol[1]` there.
- **How far the two hold up.** These checks were designed after the two genes were seen, and they can only weaken a result. With Y status shuffled within stratum in every source at once, `r ng_num(ng_extra$permutation_shuffles[1])` times, the permutation p is `r pv(ng_extra$permutation_p[1])` for `r ng_extra$symbol[1]` and `r pv(ng_extra$permutation_p[2])` for `r ng_extra$symbol[2]`; to stay hits at their ranks they need p below `r pv(ng_extra$bh_cut[1])` and `r pv(ng_extra$bh_cut[2])`. `r ng_both(ng_extra$permutation_below_cut, "stay below", "stays below")``r if (length(ng_unresolved) > 0) sprintf(" For %s the margin is smaller than the shuffles can resolve.", ext_list(ng_unresolved)) else ""` With any one of the `r ng_cfu(ng_extra$symbol[1], "largest p", "n")` models left out, the largest p is `r pv(ng_extra$leave_one_out_largest_p[1])` and `r pv(ng_extra$leave_one_out_largest_p[2])`. `r ng_both(ng_extra$leave_one_out_below_cut, "stay below their cut", "stays below its cut")` The sign holds with RNA-only and with DNA-confirmed Y calls. NextGen's unadjusted estimate is what carries both over the line. With two sources their FDR was `r r2(ng_extra$two_source_fdr[1])` and `r r2(ng_extra$two_source_fdr[2])`. With screen quality in NextGen's model the three-source FDR is `r f3(ng_extra$fdr_nextgen_with_screen_quality[1])` and `r r2(ng_extra$fdr_nextgen_with_screen_quality[2])`; with genome doubling, TP53 and aneuploidy in NextGen's model, `r r2(ng_extra$fdr_nextgen_with_genomic_covariates[1])` and `r r2(ng_extra$fdr_nextgen_with_genomic_covariates[2])`; with every source's adjusted model, `r r2(ng_extra$fdr_every_source_adjusted[1])` and `r r2(ng_extra$fdr_every_source_adjusted[2])`. RNAi shows neither (p = `r r2(ng_extra$rnai_p[1])` and `r r2(ng_extra$rnai_p[2])`). `r ng_extra$symbol[1]` is a small, consistent shift that passes only with NextGen's unadjusted estimate, and `r ng_extra$symbol[2]` is borderline. Neither is reported as a finding.
- **Inside oesophagogastric adenocarcinoma, still no gene.** With NextGen as a third source inside this cancer type, `r num(nrow(ng_oes_rows))` genes are tested and `r ext_count_word(sum(ng_oes_rows$combined_hit))` passes. `r ng_oes_best$symbol` comes closest (FDR `r r2(ng_oes_best$combined_fdr)`, from `r r2(ng_oes_best$two_source_fdr)` with two sources). Colorectal cancer stays as reported, because NextGen has only `r ng_n(ng_bowel, 1)` Y-negative and `r ng_n(ng_bowel, 0)` Y-positive bowel models, below the gate of five per group.
- **Pancreas, the sources pooled.** Pancreas is the one cancer type that no source can test alone and the sources together can: the cell lines have `r ng_in("Pancreas", "Cell lines", "n_negative")` Y-negative and `r ng_in("Pancreas", "Cell lines", "n_positive")` Y-positive lines, and NextGen `r ng_in("Pancreas", "NextGen", "n_negative")` and `r ng_in("Pancreas", "NextGen", "n_positive")` models. The cell lines alone had been tested inside pancreas before, with none of the four paired genes significant (p = `r r2(min(ng_before$p))` to `r r2(max(ng_before$p))`; Figure 3b). New here are the NextGen models and a pooled test. It ranks the scores within each source and compares the Y groups within strata, the screening library in the cell lines and the screen format in NextGen. All Y-positive pancreatic cell lines sit in one library, so the comparison is `r ng_pn(ng_names[1], "Cell lines")$n_negative` against `r ng_pn(ng_names[1], "Cell lines")$n_positive` lines there and `r ng_pn(ng_names[1], "NextGen")$n_negative` against `r ng_pn(ng_names[1], "NextGen")$n_positive` NextGen models. The p-value counts every arrangement of Y status within strata, `r num(ng_pool$arrangements)` in all. `r ext_list(ng_pool_holds)` show the Y effect inside pancreas (p = `r ext_list(pv(ng_pooled_named[source == "Pooled"][match(ng_pool_holds, symbol), p]))`; BH among the four), with differences of `r ext_list(r2(ng_pooled_named[source == "Pooled"][match(ng_pool_holds, symbol), estimate_chronos]))` Chronos units, and `r ext_list(ng_pool_fails)` does not (p = `r r2(ng_pn(ng_pool_fails[1])$p)`) (Figure 13e). The cell-line half of the test is not independent of the scan that named these genes, because its `r ng_pn(ng_names[1], "Cell lines")[, n_negative + n_positive]` lines were part of that scan. The NextGen half is, and alone it gives p = `r ext_list(f3(ng_pooled_named[source == "NextGen"][match(ng_pool_holds, symbol), p]))` for the three genes, where `r f3(ng_pn(ng_names[1], "NextGen")$floor)` is the smallest value its models can give. The result shows that the effect is present inside pancreas, not that it is specific to pancreas.
- **A single gene cannot be called genome-wide in pancreas.** With `r ng_pn(ng_names[1])$n_negative` against `r ng_pn(ng_names[1])$n_positive` models, the smallest p-value the exact test can give is `r pv(ng_pool$floor)`, and one discovery among `r num(ng_pool$genes)` genes would need `r pv(ng_pool$bh_critical_p)`. BH could pass genes only if at least `r ceiling(ng_pooled_all$floor[1] * nrow(ng_pooled_all) / 0.05)` of them sat at that smallest value together; `r sum(ng_pooled_all$p <= ng_pooled_all$floor * (1 + 1e-9))` `r if (sum(ng_pooled_all$p <= ng_pooled_all$floor * (1 + 1e-9)) == 1) "gene sits" else "genes sit"` there. The smallest family-wise p over all genes is `r r2(ng_pool$min_family_wise_p)`. The table is a ranking, and no gene is called from it (Figure 13f).
- **The paired genes inside three more lineages.** A secondary table pools the sources the same way in bowel, oesophagus/stomach and brain, where single sources can already test. All four genes have p below 0.05 in each of the three; the largest is `r f3(ng_weakest$p)`, for `r ng_weakest$symbol` in `r ng_lineage(ng_weakest$type)`. No call rests on that table.
- **Models screened at both institutes.** Donors that Sanger also screened gave `r nrow(ng_shared)` NextGen models, `r sum(ng_shared$sex == "Male")` of them male, each under the same model name at both institutes. Where both have a Y call, the calls agree for `r sum(ng_shared$calls_agree, na.rm = TRUE)` of `r sum(!is.na(ng_shared$calls_agree))`. The exception is `r ng_disagree$name`: Y-positive at Sanger, with all seven Y genes expressed and chrY kept in DNA, and Y-negative at the Broad, with no Y expression and no chrY in DNA. Y status belongs to the culture, not to the donor or the model name. The dependency profiles of two screens of one model share little (median rank correlation `r r2(ng_comb$shared_donors$profile_median)` against `r r2(ng_comb$shared_donors$unrelated_median)` for unrelated models of the same lineage), though `r ng_comb$shared_donors$above_unrelated_q95` of the `r ng_comb$shared_donors$compared` pairs are above the unrelated 95th percentile. That is one reason why sources are combined through test statistics or ranks within a source, never as raw scores.

## What NextGen adds

```{r ng-power}
ng_power_tab <- ng_power[, .(Test = sub(" adenocarcinoma$", "", analysis), Source = source, Models = ext_pair(n_negative, n_positive), `Named gene` = r2(named),
  `Genome-wide` = ifelse(is.na(genome_wide), "not possible", r2(genome_wide)))]
show(ng_power_tab, align = "lllll",
  caption = "Best-case effect found 80% of the time, in SD of a gene's spread between models (rank SD for the pooled test), from each fitted design. Models: Y-negative / Y-positive. Named gene: one test at p < 0.05. Genome-wide: one more discovery in the family as tested; in NextGen alone it must also clear the bar from the shuffles. Two sources: cell lines and Sanger organoids, as in the section above.")
```

- **Three of the four paired genes now hold outside the cell lines.** DDX3X and RPS4X hold in both organoid sources, and EIF1AX in NextGen, its only independent test. ZFX is not confirmed: it is absent in the Sanger organoids and borderline in NextGen.
- **Pooling three sources adds no vulnerability.** The two extra genes that cross FDR 0.05, `r ext_list(ng_extra$symbol)`, are small shifts that depend on NextGen's unadjusted estimates. `r ng_extra$symbol[1]` is less needed with Y loss, and `r ng_extra$symbol[2]` is not a dependency.
- **Inside pancreas the paired genes reach significance,** `r length(ng_pool_holds)` of the four, once the cell lines are pooled with NextGen; the cell lines alone had not shown it.
- **No cancer-type-specific vulnerability appears.** With three sources the effect detectable genome-wide falls from `r r2(ng_pw(ng_oes, "Two sources")$genome_wide)` to `r r2(ng_pw(ng_oes, "Three sources")$genome_wide)` SD in oesophagogastric cancer and from `r r2(ng_pw("All cancer types", "Two sources")$genome_wide)` to `r r2(ng_pw("All cancer types", "Three sources")$genome_wide)` SD for all cancer types together; NextGen alone finds `r r2(ng_pw("All cancer types", "NextGen")$genome_wide)` SD at best. These are best-case figures, and every other cancer type stays where the power analysis left it.

# Driver status inside cancer types

```{r fig14}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig14_driver_type.png")
```

The context screen tests each driver alteration across all cancer types at once. This section, added on 2026-10-06, asks a finer question: inside one cancer type, does Y loss create a dependency among the lines that carry a given driver alteration, and does that differ from the lines of the same type without it? Its main result is a limit and not a hit. Few such questions can be posed with the lines that exist, and those that can be posed would need large effects. A gene counts as altered in a line with any of a driver-flagged mutation, an amplification or a deep deletion. A split is a gene in a cancer type with at least `r dt_word(dt_gate)` altered lines in each Y group.

The lines, the statuses, the splits and the gene families were frozen before any gene was compared with Y status inside a split, with one exception: a trial run printed three estimates for one paired gene in one split, and nothing was changed because of it. An independent review of the first full run led to four additions, each marked below as added after the review: least-squares p-values beside the test's own, a bar for the difference by driver status in a gene named in advance, a limit for a test on the Chronos scale, and a second way to size a known effect.

```{r dt-overview}
dt_any <- function(rows) sum(rows$inside_only > 0 | rows$specific > 0)
dt_overview <- rbind(
  data.table(Screen = "Cell lines, Y effect among altered lines", Splits = nrow(dt_splits), Tests = num(dt_tests$inside_tests), Passing = ext_count_word(dt_tests$inside_only + dt_tests$calls), Shuffled = dt_shuffled(dt_any(dt_null_cells))),
  data.table(Screen = "Cell lines, difference by driver status", Splits = nrow(dt_four), Tests = num(dt_tests$interaction_tests), Passing = ext_count_word(dt_tests$calls), Shuffled = dt_shuffled(sum(dt_null_cells$specific > 0))),
  data.table(Screen = "Cell lines, the four paired genes", Splits = nrow(dt_splits), Tests = num(nrow(dt_paired)), Passing = as.character(sum(dt_paired$shown)), Shuffled = dt_shuffled(sum(dt_null_cells$named_shown > 0))),
  data.table(Screen = "Sanger organoids, Y effect among altered organoids", Splits = nrow(dt_org_splits), Tests = num(nrow(dt_org)), Passing = ext_count_word(sum(dt_org$specific | dt_org$inside_only)), Shuffled = dt_shuffled(dt_any(dt_null_org))),
  data.table(Screen = "Sanger organoids, difference by driver status", Splits = dt_org_splits[label == "specificity testable", .N], Tests = num(sum(is.finite(dt_org$interaction_p))), Passing = ext_count_word(sum(dt_org$specific)), Shuffled = dt_shuffled(sum(dt_null_org$specific > 0))),
  data.table(Screen = "Cell lines and organoids combined", Splits = nrow(dt_pairs), Tests = num(nrow(dt_comb)), Passing = ext_count_word(sum(dt_comb$combined_hit)), Shuffled = "not run")
)
show(dt_overview, align = "lrlll",
  caption = sprintf("The tests of this section, by the rule fixed in advance. A split is a driver gene in a cancer type with %d altered models per Y group. Passing: tests at FDR 0.05 over all tests of the row; the four paired genes are a family named in advance, and a test passes when the gene is seen among the altered lines. Shuffled: runs out of %d with Y status shuffled within driver status that gave at least one passing test.", dt_gate, dt_runs))
```

## What can be tested

- **Few pairs of a gene and a cancer type have the lines.** Among the `r num(dt_tests$lines)` male lines with a screen, `r num(dt_prep$genes_altered)` genes are altered in at least one. That gives `r num(dt_cells("lineage")$pairs)` pairs of a gene and a lineage with an altered line. Both Y groups are present among the altered lines in `r num(dt_cells("lineage")$both_y_groups)` of them, `r dt_cells("lineage")$at_least_5` have `r dt_word(dt_gate)` altered lines per Y group, and `r dt_cells("lineage")$all_four_cells` also have `r dt_word(dt_gate)` unaltered lines per Y group, which a test of a difference by driver status needs (Figure 14a). At disease level the last two counts are `r dt_cells("disease")$at_least_5` and `r dt_cells("disease")$all_four_cells`, at subtype level `r dt_cells("subtype")$at_least_5` and `r dt_cells("subtype")$all_four_cells`.
- **The testable splits are small and sit in a few genes.** Over the three levels there are `r nrow(dt_splits)` distinct splits in `r uniqueN(dt_splits$type)` cancer types; a split with the same lines at two levels is counted once. They involve `r uniqueN(dt_splits$gene)` genes (`r ext_list(dt_gene_order)`), and TP53 alone accounts for `r dt_splits[gene == "TP53", .N]`. In `r sum(dt_smaller < 10)` of the `r nrow(dt_splits)` the smaller altered cell has fewer than ten lines (Figure 14b). Many splits share most of their lines: together they hold `r dt_prep$splits$altered_sets` different sets of altered lines, which fall into `r dt_prep$splits$shared_groups` groups once sets that share `r dt_pct(dt_set$shared_lines_fraction)`% of their lines are joined. CDKN2A, CDKN2B and MTAP often mark the same lines, because one deletion removes all three.
- **A difference by driver status can be tested in `r nrow(dt_four)` splits.** At lineage level these are in `r dt_by_type(dt_four[level == "lineage"])`. KRAS-altered lung is one of them, with `r dt_split("KRAS", "Lung")$neg_alt` Y-negative and `r dt_split("KRAS", "Lung")$pos_alt` Y-positive altered lines.
- **Screening library takes part of what is left.** Inside a small split, library can follow Y status. Fitted on its altered lines alone, as the context screen fits a context, the worst split (`r dt_worst_alone$gene` in `r dt_name(dt_worst_alone$type)`) keeps `r dt_pct(dt_worst_alone$kept_inside_alone)`% of the information of a plain two-group comparison, and `r dt_prep$splits$kept_alone_below_flag` splits keep under `r dt_pct(dt_set$information_flag)`%. Each split is therefore fitted as one model on all lines of its cancer type, with library, driver status, and a Y effect for the altered and for the unaltered lines. That keeps `r dt_pct(dt_prep$splits$kept_inside_median)`% in the median split and `r dt_pct(dt_prep$splits$kept_inside_min)`% in the worst.
- **In `r sum(!dt_info$robust_reachable)` splits a result could have been called robust only by luck.** The robustness rule fixed for all added models asks for a permutation p-value below `r dt_set$robust_permutation_p`. In the smallest splits so few arrangements of Y status exist that the shuffles do not, on average, give one even for the most extreme arrangement. No result in those splits passed the rule.
- **Organoids and NextGen.** The Sanger organoids have `r nrow(dt_org_splits)` splits (`r ext_list(dt_org_splits[, sprintf("%s in %s", gene, dt_name(type))])`), `r dt_org_splits[label == "specificity testable", .N]` of them with the test of a difference. NextGen has none: its closest pair is `r dt_nextgen$gene` in `r dt_name(dt_nextgen$type)`, with `r dt_nextgen$neg_alt` Y-negative and `r dt_nextgen$pos_alt` Y-positive altered models. `r tools::toTitleCase(dt_word(nrow(dt_pairs)))` colorectal splits (`r ext_list(dt_pairs$gene)`) exist in both the cell lines and the organoids and are combined.

## What a split could detect

The limits come from the tests themselves, as in the power analysis of the cancer-type tests. A real selective gene is shifted towards more dependent in the Y-negative altered lines of one split and tested as the one gene added to that split's fit. Shifts are in units of a gene's spread between lines (SD), and a shift counts as detectable when it is found `r dt_pct(dt_target)`% of the time. The stored p-values of all `r dt_power$splits` splits were reproduced exactly before simulating, and real genes sent through the simulation's own path came back with their stored p-values.

These are limits of the layer's test: limma's moderated t on scores ranked over all lines, the test of the context screen. Two of its properties matter here. Ranks cap how far a few lines can move, so detection levels off below `r dt_pct(dt_target)`% in small splits however large the shift. And at these sizes the test takes a gene's variance almost wholly from the other genes: the borrowed information weighs `r round(median(dt_prior_df))` degrees of freedom in the median split, against `r min(dt_info$df_new)` to `r max(dt_info$df_new)` of a split's own.

- **One gene named in advance.** At p < 0.05 every split finds a shift, of `r r2(median(dt_lim("candidate")$limit))` SD in the median split (`r r2(min(dt_lim("candidate")$limit))` in the largest, `r r2(max(dt_lim("candidate")$limit))` in the weakest) (Figure 14c). Normal theory on the design agrees with the simulation here (ratio `r r2(min(dt_ratio("candidate")))` to `r r2(max(dt_ratio("candidate")))`). The four paired genes themselves reach p < 0.05 in `r dt_pct(dt_paired[, mean(inside_p < 0.05 & inside_rank < 0)])`% of their `r nrow(dt_paired)` tests inside splits.
- **The split searched alone,** over its `r num(dt_tests$selective)` genes: `r dt_reach("split_alone")` of the `r nrow(dt_splits)` splits find a shift, of `r r2(median(dt_lim("split_alone")$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD in the median of those.
- **The whole layer.** One more discovery among the `r num(dt_tests$inside_tests)` tests needs a p-value below `r dt_sci(dt_tests$bars$family_inside)`. `r dt_reach("family")` splits reach that, at `r r2(median(dt_fam$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD in the median. The other `r nrow(dt_splits) - dt_reach("family")` do not reach `r dt_pct(dt_target)`% at any shift up to `r dt_largest_shift` SD: at `r dt_largest_shift` SD they find the shift in `r dt_pct(min(dt_fam[reachable == FALSE, ceiling]))`% to `r dt_pct(max(dt_fam[reachable == FALSE, ceiling]))`% of simulations, `r dt_pct(median(dt_fam[reachable == FALSE, ceiling]))`% in the median. None of the `r dt_fam[smaller == dt_gate, .N]` splits with `r dt_word(dt_gate)` lines in the smaller altered cell reaches `r dt_pct(dt_target)`%, and all `r dt_fam[smaller >= 10, .N]` with ten or more do. At sizes like those of known effects a search finds little: a shift of `r dt_sizes[1]` SD is found in `r dt_pct(median(dt_at(dt_sizes[1], "family")))`% of simulations in the median split and one of `r dt_sizes[2]` SD in `r dt_pct(median(dt_at(dt_sizes[2], "family")))`%.
- **A test on the Chronos scale has no such ceiling** (added after the review). Plain least squares on Chronos scores, each gene with its own variance, reaches the layer's bar in `r dt_raw[, sum(reachable)]` of the `r nrow(dt_raw)` splits, at `r r2(median(dt_raw$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD in the median and `r r2(median(dt_raw[smaller == dt_gate, limit], na.rm = TRUE))` SD in the splits with `r dt_word(dt_gate)` lines in the smaller altered cell. That test is not calibrated in cells this small, which is why the layer does not use it: the raw-scale p-values stored beside the Chronos estimates give `r sum(dt_raw_fdr < 0.05)` tests at FDR 0.05, `r sum(dt_raw_fdr < 0.05 & !dt_screen$symbol %in% hit_symbols)` of them outside the paired genes and all of those in splits with at most `r dt_screen[dt_raw_fdr < 0.05 & !symbol %in% hit_symbols, max(pmin(n_neg_in, n_pos_in))]` lines in the smaller cell. So "no shift is enough" describes the rank-based test, and on any scale a search needs shifts of several SD.
- **A difference by driver status** needs the Y effect to differ from the unaltered lines of the same cancer type. For one gene named in advance, at p < 0.05, `r dt_named_difference[, sum(reachable)]` of the `r nrow(dt_named_difference)` splits that can test it find a difference `r dt_pct(dt_target)`% of the time, of `r r2(median(dt_named_difference$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD in the median (`r r2(min(dt_named_difference$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` to `r r2(max(dt_named_difference$limit, na.rm = TRUE))`); this bar was added after the review. In a search, where the layer's rule asks for the effect among altered lines and for the difference, `r ext_count_word(dt_reach("specificity"))` of the `r nrow(dt_four)` splits reaches `r dt_pct(dt_target)`%: at `r dt_largest_shift` SD the best split (`r dt_lim("specificity")[which.max(ceiling), sprintf("%s in %s", gene, dt_name(type))]`) finds the difference in `r dt_pct(max(dt_lim("specificity")$ceiling))`% of simulations and the median split in `r dt_pct(median(dt_lim("specificity")$ceiling))`%.

```{r dt-known}
dt_known_tab <- rbindlist(lapply(dt_shown_refs, function(ref) {
  data.table(`Effect as large as` = dt_short(ref), Chronos = r2(dt_ref(ref, "own spread")$effect_chronos),
    `SD, own spread` = dt_r1(dt_ref(ref, "own spread")$effect_sd), `SD, typical gene` = dt_r1(dt_ref(ref, "typical gene")$effect_sd),
    `Named: gene itself` = dt_found(ref, "own gene", "candidate"), `Named: typical gene` = dt_found(ref, "typical gene", "candidate"),
    `Search: gene itself` = dt_found(ref, "own gene", "family"), `Search: typical gene` = dt_found(ref, "typical gene", "family"))
}))
show(dt_known_tab[order(-as.numeric(`SD, own spread`))], align = "lrrrrrrr",
  caption = sprintf("Known effects moved into each split's Y-negative altered lines: the number of splits, out of %d, in which the effect is found %s%% of the time, as a gene named in advance and in a search over the layer. Gene itself: a resampled copy of the gene, with its own spread. Typical gene: the same Chronos shift on an ordinary selective gene (typical spread %s Chronos units). SD: the effect over the gene's own spread, and over the typical spread. DDX3X, EIF1AX, ZFX and RPS4X: their effect in Y-negative lines.",
    nrow(dt_splits), dt_pct(dt_target), r2(dt_power$host_sd)))
```

- **How large a known effect is depends on the gene** (the second way of sizing was added after the review). DDX3X's effect is `r r2(dt_ref("DDX3X in Y-negative", "own spread")$effect_chronos)` Chronos units. That is `r dt_r1(dt_ref("DDX3X in Y-negative", "own spread")$effect_sd)` SD of DDX3X's own spread and `r dt_r1(dt_ref("DDX3X in Y-negative", "typical gene")$effect_sd)` SD of a typical selective gene's, because the paired genes vary far more between lines than most genes do. A new vulnerability could be either kind of gene, so the table gives both.
- **A search would have missed most known effects.** As a copy of the gene itself, an effect like DDX3X's is found by a search over the layer in `r ext_count_word(dt_found("DDX3X in Y-negative", "own gene", "family"))` of the `r nrow(dt_splits)` splits; the same Chronos shift on a typical gene is found in `r dt_found("DDX3X in Y-negative", "typical gene", "family")`. For KRAS dependence in KRAS-driven lines the counts are `r dt_found("KRAS in KRAS-driver", "own gene", "family")` and `r dt_found("KRAS in KRAS-driver", "typical gene", "family")`, and for WRN dependence in MSI lines, the best-known synthetic-lethal pair, `r ext_count_word(dt_found("WRN in MSI", "own gene", "family"))` and `r ext_count_word(dt_found("WRN in MSI", "typical gene", "family"))`.

## Lines needed

How much larger would the collection have to be for the layer's test? Each split's design was copied `r ext_list(dt_multiples[-1])` times, every copy carrying the spread of a different real gene, and the same shifts were tested at the same bars. This keeps the share of Y loss, the mix of libraries and the behaviour of ranks. The bar and the variance prior are held at today's values; a larger collection would also test more splits, so the true requirement is somewhat higher.

```{r dt-needed}
dt_need_tab <- rbindlist(lapply(sort(unique(dt_needed[convention == "size", effect_sd])), function(size) {
  layer <- dt_buckets(dt_size(size, "family"))
  difference <- dt_buckets(dt_size(size, "specificity"))
  data.table(`Shift (SD)` = formatC(size, format = "g"), Today = layer$today, `Up to 4 times` = layer$within_4, `Up to 16 times` = layer$within_16, `More` = layer$beyond,
    `Median multiple` = dt_multiple(layer$median, layer$bound), `Difference: median multiple` = dt_multiple(difference$median, difference$bound), `Difference: more` = difference$beyond)
}))
show(dt_need_tab, align = "rrrrrrrr",
  caption = sprintf("Lines needed to find a shift of a given size %s%% of the time at the layer's bar. Today, Up to 4 times, Up to %d times, More: the number of splits, out of %d, that would find it with that multiple of today's lines (cumulative). Median multiple: over the splits; \"at most\" where the median could not be read between two simulated sizes. Difference: the rule that also needs the difference from unaltered lines, over the %d splits that can test it.",
    dt_pct(dt_target), max(dt_multiples), nrow(dt_splits), nrow(dt_four)))
```

- **It depends on how variable the gene is.** For a gene as variable as the paired genes, whose effects are `r dt_r1(dt_paired_own[1])` to `r dt_r1(dt_paired_own[2])` SD of their own spread, the median split needs `r dt_multiple(min(dt_paired_multiples("own spread")))` to `r dt_multiple(max(dt_paired_multiples("own spread")))` times today's lines. The same Chronos shifts on a typical gene are `r dt_r1(dt_paired_typical[1])` to `r dt_r1(dt_paired_typical[2])` SD. The median split then needs `r dt_median(dt_known("ZFX in Y-negative", "typical gene"))` times its lines for a shift like ZFX's and `r dt_median(dt_known("DDX3X in Y-negative", "typical gene"))` times for one like DDX3X's, which `r dt_buckets(dt_known("DDX3X in Y-negative", "typical gene"))$today` of the `r nrow(dt_splits)` splits would find today (Figure 14d).
- **A difference by driver status needs more:** `r dt_median(dt_size(dt_sizes[1], "specificity"))` times for a difference of `r dt_sizes[1]` SD in the median split, against `r dt_median(dt_size(dt_sizes[1], "family"))` for the Y effect among altered lines; for a difference of `r dt_sizes[3]` SD, `r dt_buckets(dt_size(dt_sizes[3], "specificity"))$beyond` of the `r nrow(dt_four)` splits need more than `r max(dt_multiples)` times.
- **These are multiples of splits that already hold `r dt_word(dt_gate)` lines per cell.** The other `r num(dt_cells("lineage")$pairs - dt_cells("lineage")$at_least_5)` gene-by-lineage pairs start from fewer.
- **Check on real lines.** If copies stand in for lines, a real split cut to a half and copied twice should find what the whole split finds. The `r dt_cut[fraction == 0.5, uniqueN(split_id)]` largest sets of altered lines were cut `r dt_cut$repeats[1]` times each, and the largest also to a quarter. At the layer's bar the copied split's limit differs from the real split's by `r dt_signed(mean(dt_compared_at("family")$copied_against_real_log2))`% on average (`r dt_signed(min(dt_compared_at("family")$copied_against_real_log2))`% to `r dt_signed(max(dt_compared_at("family")$copied_against_real_log2))`% over `r nrow(dt_compared_at("family"))` comparisons), and for a gene named in advance by `r dt_signed(mean(dt_compared_at("candidate")$copied_against_real_log2))`% (`r dt_signed(min(dt_compared_at("candidate")$copied_against_real_log2))`% to `r dt_signed(max(dt_compared_at("candidate")$copied_against_real_log2))`%). A negative figure means that copies find smaller shifts than real lines do. So copies stand in for lines to within about `r formatC(100 * (2^max(abs(dt_compared$copied_against_real_log2)) - 1), format = "f", digits = 0)`% of a limit, and at the layer's bar the multiples above are, if anything, somewhat too low, on top of the bar being held fixed.

## What the tests show

- **Controls.** Before any Y result was read, known driver dependencies were tested inside single cancer types, on the same lines and statuses, by least squares on Chronos scores. KRAS is more needed in KRAS-altered lines inside lung (`r r2(dt_control("KRAS.*Lung")$estimate)` Chronos units, p = `r pv(dt_control("KRAS.*Lung")$p)`) and inside bowel (`r r2(dt_control("KRAS.*Bowel")$estimate)`, p = `r pv(dt_control("KRAS.*Bowel")$p)`); MDM2 is less needed in TP53-altered lines inside CNS/brain (`r r2(dt_control("MDM2.*CNS")$estimate)`, p = `r pv(dt_control("MDM2.*CNS")$p)`) and lymphoid (`r r2(dt_control("MDM2.*Lymphoid")$estimate)`, p = `r pv(dt_control("MDM2.*Lymphoid")$p)`).
- **No gene's Y effect differs by driver status inside a cancer type.** Of `r num(dt_tests$inside_tests)` tests of the Y effect among altered lines and `r num(dt_tests$interaction_tests)` tests of its difference from the unaltered lines, `r ext_count_word(dt_tests$inside_only + dt_tests$calls)` passes FDR 0.05. The smallest p-value among altered lines is `r dt_sci(dt_top$inside_p)` (FDR `r r2(dt_top$inside_fdr)`), for `r dt_top$symbol` among `r dt_top$gene`-altered `r dt_name(dt_top$type)` lines; the smallest for a difference is `r dt_sci(dt_top_difference$interaction_p)` (FDR `r r2(dt_top_difference$interaction_fdr)`).
- **The smallest p-values belong to the four paired genes.** `r nrow(dt_small)` tests are below `r formatC(dt_small_cut, format = "e", digits = 0)`. They are `r nrow(dt_distinct(dt_small))` distinct tests, because two splits at different levels hold the same altered lines, and `r nrow(dt_distinct(dt_small[symbol %in% hit_symbols]))` of those are `r ext_list(hit_symbols)` (Figure 14f). The others are `r ext_list(dt_other[, sprintf("%s among %s-altered %s lines", symbol, gene, dt_name(type))])`; both point towards less dependence with Y loss and neither passes (FDR `r r2(min(dt_other$inside_fdr))` and `r r2(max(dt_other$inside_fdr))`).
- **By least squares, the layer finds DDX3X and EIF1AX in its largest splits and nothing else** (added after the review). Because the test borrows its variance, it is conservative for a gene with little spread and generous for one with much. With each gene keeping its own variance, on the same ranks, `r nrow(dt_ols)` tests pass FDR 0.05, all of them `r ext_list(sort(unique(dt_ols$symbol)))`, in `r ext_list(unique(dt_name(dt_ols$type)))`; no other gene passes, and no difference by driver status does. Shuffled Y status gives such a test in `r dt_shuffled(sum(dt_null_cells$ols_fdr_hits > 0))` runs. For `r dt_top$symbol` in `r dt_name(dt_ols[order(inside_p_ols)][1, type])` the least-squares p-value is `r dt_sci(min(dt_ols$inside_p_ols))`, and the two genes outside the four fall to `r dt_sci(min(dt_other$inside_p_ols))` and `r dt_sci(max(dt_other$inside_p_ols))`. These p-values describe; the rule fixed in advance makes the calls.
- **The paired genes behave inside splits as they do everywhere, and show what size costs.** Judged as a family named in advance, they are seen in `r sum(dt_paired$shown)` of `r nrow(dt_paired)` tests: in `r dt_seen(function(n) n == dt_gate)`% of those with `r dt_word(dt_gate)` lines in the smaller altered cell, `r dt_seen(function(n) n %in% 6:7)`% with six or seven, `r dt_seen(function(n) n %in% 8:9)`% with eight or nine and `r dt_seen(function(n) n >= 10)`% with ten or more (Figure 14e). `r dt_paired[symbol == "DDX3X", sum(inside < 0)]` of `r dt_paired[symbol == "DDX3X", .N]` DDX3X estimates are negative. In no split does a paired gene's effect differ by driver status: over the `r nrow(dt_paired_difference)` such tests the smallest p-value is `r f3(min(dt_paired_difference$interaction_p))` (FDR `r r2(min(dt_paired_difference$difference_fdr))`), and these tests could have shown a difference of about `r r2(median(dt_named_difference$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD. Of the `r nrow(dt_follow)` tests where a paired gene is seen, `r sum(dt_follow$robust)` pass the robustness rule.
- **Shuffled Y status.** Over `r dt_runs` shuffles within driver status, `r dt_r1(100 * mean(dt_null_cells$inside_below_0.05))`% of p-values among altered lines are below 0.05 and the inflation factor averages `r r2(mean(dt_null_cells$inside_lambda))`. `r dt_shuffled(sum(dt_null_cells$specific > 0))` runs gave a difference by driver status and `r dt_shuffled(sum(dt_null_cells$inside_only > 0))` a gene among altered lines. The shuffles show that the test is sound on average over genes; they do not check it gene by gene, and they say nothing about confounding.
- **Organoids and the combination.** None of the `r num(nrow(dt_org))` tests among altered organoids passes, nor any of the `r num(nrow(dt_comb))` combined tests in the `r dt_word(nrow(dt_pairs))` colorectal splits. `r if (dt_org[order(inside_p)][1, symbol] == dt_comb[order(combined_p)][1, symbol]) sprintf("%s is the top gene in both", dt_org[order(inside_p)][1, symbol]) else sprintf("The top genes are %s and %s", dt_org[order(inside_p)][1, symbol], dt_comb[order(combined_p)][1, symbol])` (p = `r dt_sci(min(dt_org$inside_p))` in the organoids and `r dt_sci(min(dt_comb$combined_p))` in the combination), and by least squares `r ext_list(sort(unique(dt_ols_org$symbol)))` passes in `r nrow(dt_ols_org)` organoid splits. From their designs alone, the organoid splits could find `r dt_r1(min(dt_org_best[bar == "family", best_case_sd]))` to `r dt_r1(max(dt_org_best[bar == "family", best_case_sd]))` SD in a search and the combined splits `r dt_r1(min(dt_comb_best[bar == "family", best_case_sd]))` to `r dt_r1(max(dt_comb_best[bar == "family", best_case_sd]))` SD; these are best cases that ignore what ranks cost on few models.

## What this layer shows

- **The question can rarely be posed.** `r dt_cells("lineage")$at_least_5` of `r num(dt_cells("lineage")$pairs)` gene-by-lineage pairs have the lines for a Y effect among altered lines, and `r dt_cells("lineage")$all_four_cells` for a difference by driver status.
- **Where it can be posed, a gene named in advance can be tested and a search sees only large shifts.** A named gene needs about `r dt_r1(median(dt_lim("candidate")$limit))` SD for the Y effect among altered lines and about `r dt_r1(median(dt_named_difference$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD for a difference by driver status. A search needs `r dt_r1(median(dt_fam$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD in the `r dt_reach("family")` splits where the layer's test reaches `r dt_pct(dt_target)`% at all, and about `r dt_r1(median(dt_raw$limit, na.rm = TRUE))` SD by a test on the Chronos scale.
- **The tests agree with the rest of this report.** Nothing passes the rule, and the strongest signals inside the splits are the four paired genes.
- **More cell lines of the same kind would have to be several times as many.** For effects like the known ones the median split needs `r dt_median(dt_known("DDX3X in Y-negative", "typical gene"))` to `r dt_median(dt_known("ZFX in Y-negative", "typical gene"))` times its lines when the gene is of typical spread, and `r dt_multiple(min(dt_paired_multiples("own spread")))` to `r dt_multiple(max(dt_paired_multiples("own spread")))` times when it is as variable as the paired genes; a difference by driver status needs more.

# Expression

## Which genes' expression goes with each dependency

```{r fig7}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig7_expression_and_dependency.png")
```

```{r attribution}
show(paired[match(hit_symbols, dependency), .(Dependency = dependency, `Paired Y gene` = y_gene, `Joint-model p` = pv(joint_p), `p within Y-positive lines` = pv(within_positive_p))],
  caption = "The paired Y gene for each hit. Joint model: all seven Y genes together, lineage and library adjusted, on every eligible male with CRISPR and RNA.")
```

- **The paired Y gene is the one that matters.** Whole-Y loss removes all seven genes at once, so the two-group comparison cannot say which gene is responsible. The partial-deletion lines can: with all seven Y genes in one model, the paired gene is the strongest term for each of the four dependencies. Neighbouring Y genes that are lost together with it (for example UTY with DDX3Y, KDM5D with EIF1AY) carry part of the same signal, so this localises each effect to a gene or a short stretch of the Y rather than proving a single gene.
- **The relationship is graded.** Among lines that still express the Y, lower expression of DDX3Y, EIF1AY and RPS4Y1 goes with stronger dependency on the X partner (p-values in the table); for ZFY the within-group trend is weak.
- **Beyond Y status there is little.** After adjusting for lineage and Y status, the number of non-Y genes associated with each dependency at FDR 0.05 is `r paste(sprintf("%s %d", hit_symbols, dep_summary[match(hit_symbols, dependency), adjusted_hits_not_y]), collapse = ", ")`, of `r num(dep_summary$genes[1])` expressed genes.
- **ZFX has a second buffer.** The top non-Y gene for ZFX is `r dep_summary[dependency == "ZFX", top_adjusted]` (partial r = `r r2(dep_summary[dependency == "ZFX", top_adjusted_r])`, and `r r2(dep_summary[dependency == "ZFX", top_within_negative_r])` within Y-negative lines): lines that express more of it depend less on ZFX. ZNF711 is the third member of the ZFX/ZFY zinc-finger family, so this is the same paralog logic acting from the X.

## Expression differences between the groups

```{r fig6}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig6_expression_differences.png")
```

- **Scope.** limma-voom on `r de_json$y_negative` Y-negative and `r de_json$y_positive` Y-positive lines; `r num(de_json$genes_tested)` genes with a known chromosome outside chrY form the test family. chrY genes define the call, so they are a positive control only.
- **Result.** `r de_json$de` genes pass FDR 0.05 (`r de_json$de_up` higher, `r de_json$de_down` lower in Y-negative lines); `r de_json$loy_specific` keep their sign and significance after adjustment for genome doubling, TP53 and aneuploidy.
- **Dosage control.** Expressed pseudoautosomal genes fall by a median of `r r2(abs(dosage[dosage_class == "PAR", median_log_fc]))` log2 units, against `r r2(dosage[dosage_class == "autosomal", median_log_fc])` for autosomal and `r r2(dosage[dosage_class == "chrX non-PAR", median_log_fc])` for X-linked genes outside the PAR. Losing one of two copies predicts 1.0.
- **The X partners barely compensate.** ZFX is slightly higher in Y-negative lines (log2 `r r2(de[symbol == "ZFX", log_fc])`, FDR `r formatC(de[symbol == "ZFX", fdr], format = "f", digits = 3)`); DDX3X, RPS4X and EIF1AX lean the same way without passing (FDR `r r2(de[symbol == "DDX3X", fdr])`, `r r2(de[symbol == "RPS4X", fdr])`, `r r2(de[symbol == "EIF1AX", fdr])`). These shifts are small next to the loss of the Y copy.
- **Caution on pathways.** Several Hallmark sets shift (panel c), but whole cytobands are also enriched (`r de_json$positional_fdr` positional sets at FDR 0.05), which is the signature of co-occurring copy-number changes. Pathway shifts here describe the kind of tumour that loses its Y as much as the loss itself.
- **Overlap with the dependencies.** Testing the differentially expressed gene sets against each dependency's association ranking (Y status accounted for) gives a smallest FDR of `r r2(min(overlap[dependency %in% hit_symbols, fdr]))` across the four hits, so the genes that change with Y loss are not, as a group, the genes that track the dependencies.

# Random forests

```{r fig8}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/fig8_forests.png")
```

Forest importance has no false-discovery rate of its own, so each result below comes with two-seed stability and a matched run on shuffled labels.

```{r accuracy}
acc <- acc_wide[match(c(hit_symbols, "COMPOSITE"), dependency)]
show(acc[, .(Dependency = dependency, `Lineage + library` = r2(m0), `+ Y status` = r2(m1), `+ seven Y genes` = r2(m2), `+ all expression` = r2(m3))],
  caption = "Out-of-fold R2 of nested forests (10-fold, 3 repeats, donors kept within folds).")
```

```{r forest-numbers}
crispr_forest <- forest_y[dataset == "crispr_effect"]
stable_genes <- forest_y_genes[stable == TRUE]
given <- forest_features[strata == "given lineage" & stable == TRUE]
beyond <- forest_features[strata == "beyond Y status" & stable == TRUE]
```

- **Predicting the dependencies.** Y status carries most of what can be predicted for DDX3X and EIF1AX. For RPS4X the seven Y genes add far more than the two-group label does (R2 `r r2(acc_wide[dependency == "RPS4X", m1])` to `r r2(acc_wide[dependency == "RPS4X", m2])`): RPS4Y1 is kept in many partial deletions, and its level matters. The rest of the transcriptome adds nothing for DDX3X, EIF1AX or RPS4X, and adds `r r2(acc_wide[dependency == "ZFX", m3 - m2])` for ZFX, in line with the ZNF711 result above. COMPOSITE is the mean of the four hits. The other X partners cannot be predicted at all (R2 near zero).
- **Which expression features are selected.** With shadows shuffled within lineage, the stable features for the four hits are `r paste(sapply(hit_symbols, function(s) sprintf("%s: %s", s, { g <- given[dependency == s][order(-mean_importance), gene_symbol]; if (length(g) == 0) "none" else paste(head(g, 5), collapse = ", ") })), collapse = "; ")`. When Y status is also given to the forest and shadows are shuffled within lineage and Y status, `r nrow(beyond[dependency %in% hit_symbols])` features remain stable across the four hits`r if (nrow(beyond[dependency %in% hit_symbols]) > 0) paste0(" (", paste(unique(beyond[dependency %in% hit_symbols, paste(dependency, gene_symbol, sep = ": ")]), collapse = "; "), ")") else ""`.
- **Predicting Y status from dependencies.** A forest on `r num(crispr_forest$features)` selective dependencies separates the groups with an out-of-bag AUC of `r r2(crispr_forest$oob_auc)`, against `r r2(crispr_forest$oob_auc_lineage_only)` from lineage and library alone. `r crispr_forest$stable` genes are stable across both seeds (`r paste(head(stable_genes$symbol, 8), collapse = ", ")`), `r crispr_forest$stable_and_regression_fdr` of them regression hits; runs on shuffled labels confirmed `r gsub(";", ", ", crispr_forest$null_confirmed)` genes.
- **Predicting Y status from drugs.** In all `r sum(forest_y$dataset != "crispr_effect")` drug datasets the forest does no better than lineage alone, and no compound is stable.

# Checks on the pipeline

- **Known biology through the same code.** With the genotype as the exposure, BRAF-altered lines depend on BRAF (effect `r r2(controls[grepl("BRAF dependency", control), estimate])`, rank 1 of `r num(nrow(genes))`), KRAS-altered lines on KRAS (`r r2(controls[grepl("KRAS dependency", control), estimate])`, rank 1), and TP53-altered lines lose MDM2 dependency (`r r2(controls[grepl("MDM2 dependency", control), estimate])`, rank 1). BRAF-inhibitor sensitivity and MDM2-inhibitor resistance have the expected sign in all six drug datasets that hold such compounds, which confirms that lower means more sensitive on every metric.
- **Calibration.** With Y status shuffled within lineage, `r r2(100 * controls_json$gene_calibration$mean_fraction_below_0.05)`% of gene tests fall below 0.05 and `r controls_json$gene_calibration$permutations_with_fdr_hits` of `r controls_json$gene_calibration$permutations` shuffles give any FDR hit.
- **Inputs.** All input files match the collection's recorded checksums and dimensions; every join logs its unmatched identifiers.
- **Freeze.** Thresholds, calls, cohort and contexts were hashed before any outcome was tested against Y status. One disclosure: during design, provisional calls were checked against the X-Y partner CRISPR columns to confirm the controls were detectable; no threshold was changed afterwards.

# Comparison with the earlier analyses

```{r comparison}
show(cmp_calls[, .(`Earlier call table` = sub(" \\(.*$", "", source), `Both definite` = both_definite, Agree = agree, `Newly classified here` = newly_classified, `Definite only before` = old_only)],
  caption = "The new calls against each earlier call table (male lines).")
```

- **Calls.** Where both are definite, the new calls agree with the reviewed DNA calls in `r cmp_calls[1, agree]` of `r cmp_calls[1, both_definite]` lines, and classify `r cmp_calls[1, newly_classified]` lines that table left unresolved.
- **Lines.** The first analysis compared `r cmp_genes$old_lines` lines; this one compares `r cmp_genes$new_lines`.
- **Genes.** The first analysis's hits (`r gsub(";", ", ", cmp_genes$old_hits)`) are all recovered with far smaller FDRs. RPS4X missed FDR 0.05 in that analysis and passed in the two later ones; here it is unambiguous.
- **Earlier interaction candidates.** The two later analyses prioritised `r sum(grepl("interaction", cmp_candidates$test_type))` drug and gene interactions; `r nrow(earlier)` distinct tests have a counterpart here. None passes FDR within its context class, but `r sum(earlier$same_direction_nominal)` point the same way at a nominal p < 0.05, where chance would give about `r r2(0.025 * nrow(earlier))`: `r paste(sprintf("%s with %s (p = %s)", earlier_examples$name, sub("^.*__", "", earlier_examples$new_context), pv(earlier_examples$new_p)), collapse = "; ")`. ARHGEF2 is also this analysis's one context lead. These are the same cell lines tested again, so this is neither replication nor refutation; most earlier candidates used a continuous MSI score, which this analysis tests as MSI-high against the rest.

# Limits

- **Observational.** Y loss travels with TP53 alteration, genome doubling, aneuploidy and lineage. The four hits survive adjustment for these; a null for everything else is a null given these confounders and this sample size.
- **RNA-led calls measure Y-gene expression.** The DNA-only analysis gives the same four hits, so the findings do not depend on that choice.
- **Sex annotation.** A Y-negative line annotated male could be a mislabelled female. `r sum(calls$possible_female)` lines carry both female-like signals (XIST high and two-X copy number). Removing all XIST-high lines leaves the four gene hits unchanged; in PRISM secondary it lets `r drug_by_definition[definition == "xist_high_removed" & dataset == "prism_secondary", hits]` compounds cross FDR 0.05, within the screen-wide shift described above.
- **Guide cross-reactivity.** Guides against an X gene may also cut its Y partner, and the collection has no guide map to audit this. Cross-cutting would weaken, not create, the differences reported here.
- **Drug data.** The datasets share cell lines, use different assays and doses, and predate current culture stocks.
- **Forests.** Importance has no error rate; forest results are support for the regressions, not independent discoveries.
- **Limits of the cancer-type tests.** The detection limits are properties of the design: sample sizes, line-to-line spread and the rank-based test. They are not observed power computed from the Y results. They assume one new effect confined to one cancer type, shared by all its Y-negative lines. The benchmarks were chosen for being known, so they lean large, and some biomarkers are imperfect (MSI calls for WRN). Levels are nested, so lineage, disease and subtype are three views of the same lines.
- **Organoids, RNAi and primary AML.** The organoids are two cancer types from one study, so an effect seen there and not in cell lines may be a culture effect. Y-negative organoids have somewhat better screens; the weights and guards reduce that bias and cannot prove it gone. Organoid and Chronos scores are on different scales, so the combination uses test statistics, not effect sizes. RNAi shares most of its lines with CRISPR. In BeatAML2 the exposure is an estimate, and the signal rests on at most `r nrow(ext_aml_high)` patients (`r ext_lead$high_loss` for the one hit). Y loss is commoner with t(8;21) (`r ext_t821(TRUE)` patients with Y loss against `r ext_t821(FALSE)`), which the model adjusts for, and it does not go with age in this cohort. The response is that of a cell mixture, not of the clone without Y. Follow-up checks describe how stable a hit is; they do not confirm it.
- **DepMap NextGen.** NextGen adds `r nrow(ng_primary)` models, worth about `r round(ng_prep$design$balanced_equivalent)` per Y group once screen format and cancer type are in the model, so alone it finds only large effects. Y status there is tied to screen format, cancer type and genome doubling; the model adjusts for them and cannot separate what the data confound. In oesophagus/stomach all `r ng_n(ng_stomach, 0)` Y-positive models come from treated patients, against `r ng_treated(ng_stomach[y_negative == 1])` of `r ng_n(ng_stomach, 1)` Y-negative ones, and in pancreas all `r ng_n(ng_pancreas, 0)` Y-positive models come from one laboratory. Y-negative screens are noisier, and the weights that deal with this shift influence to fewer models. Shuffled Y status gives a gene at FDR 0.05 in `r formatC(100 * mean(ng_null$pan_fdr_hits > 0), format = "f", digits = 1)`% of runs, so the scan's p-values run small; the common-essential genes carry the excess, as noisier Y-negative screens would make them. The paired genes are therefore judged on permutation p-values, and the bar from the shuffles does not protect a discovery against the quality bias. Y status belongs to the culture: one model is Y-positive at Sanger and Y-negative at the Broad. Sex is the recorded sex. A mislabelled female would count as Y-negative and cannot be detected in these files; all four paired genes keep their sign without the `r sum(ng_primary$possible_female)` Y-negative models whose X copy number is female-like. NextGen uses a Cas12a library and the other sources Cas9, and its Chronos scores come from the manuscript's run, not the 26Q1 release. The pooled pancreas test rests on `r ng_pn(ng_names[1])$n_positive` Y-positive models and assumes that the Y effect is shared between sources in rank units. `r ext_list(ng_extra$symbol)` pass a pooled test, do not pass it once NextGen's model carries the genomic covariates, and are not reported as findings. The permutation p-values of the paired genes and the follow-up of the combined hits were added after results were seen. Each family of tests in the overview table is controlled on its own, with no correction across them, and the three-source combination is a second look at genes already tested with two sources.
- **Driver status inside cancer types.** Driver status is one yes or no per gene: it joins different alterations of a gene, and a line with a second, unlisted driver counts as unaltered. `r sum(dt_smaller < 10)` of the `r nrow(dt_splits)` splits have fewer than ten lines in a cell, so a null there says little; the limits say how little. The three levels overlap, many splits share most of their lines, and two hold the same altered lines and give the same test twice; the family counts them all. Inside a cancer type, driver status travels with subtype, other drivers, screening library and culture history, and the test of a difference cannot separate them. The test takes a gene's variance almost wholly from the other genes, so it is conservative for a quiet gene and generous for a variable one; the shuffles check it on average only. The detection limits are properties of the designs and of that test, not observed power, and the ceiling on detection in small splits belongs to the ranks. "Lines needed" assumes that added lines would look like the present ones, with the same share of Y loss, spread and libraries; it holds today's bar, and at that bar copies of a design are on average a little kinder than real lines, so it is if anything a low figure, and an order of magnitude, not a design for a screen. How large a known effect counts as depends on the spread of the gene it lands on. Reference effects were estimated in this same cohort, so the largest lean large. Organoid statuses come from the study's own table of driver events, not from the rule used for the cell lines, and the organoid limits are best cases from the designs. Four parts of the section were added after an independent review of the first full run and are marked there.
- **Unplaced genes.** `r num(de_json$genes_without_location)` genes in the count table have no chromosome in this collection and were left out of the expression test family; several behave like chrY transcripts.
